docs.text: Query and write rows ¶ Queries are explicit: nothing runs until you evaluate a query, values are bound parameters, and relations load only when you ask. Examples use the Billing models from Define models . Query rows ¶ Async Sync # inside an async operation or handler invoice = await Invoice . aget ( id = invoice_id ) maybe = await Invoice . aget_or_none ( reference = "INV-7" ) unpaid = await Invoice . filter ( customer_id = customer . id , paid = False ) . order_by ( "reference" ) first = await Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . afirst () count = await Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . acount () page = await Invoice . all () . apaginate ( PageParams ( page = 1 , page_size = 20 )) # inside a sync handler (runs in the bounded worker pool) invoice = Invoice . get ( id = invoice_id ) maybe = Invoice . get_or_none ( reference = "INV-7" ) unpaid = ( Invoice . filter ( customer_id = customer . id , paid = False ) . order_by ( "reference" ) . list () ) first = Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . first () count = Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . count () page = Invoice . all () . paginate ( PageParams ( page = 1 , page_size = 20 )) PageParams comes from hinoki.pagination . aget raises Invoice.NotFound (a 404 in a request) or MultipleObjectsReturned . Building a query ( filter , order_by , limit , offset , select_related ) issues no SQL; awaiting it or calling an evaluation method does. Filters ¶ filter(field=value) and filter(field__op=value) accept model field names and the supported comparison and membership operators ( ne , in , isnull , gt , gte , lt , lte , contains ). SQL identifiers come from model metadata. field__ne=value compiles to <> : rows where the column is NULL are not returned. Add an isnull filter when they matter. contains matches text case-insensitively and treats % , _ and \ literally. SQLite folds ASCII case only; MySQL and MariaDB assume the NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES mode is off (the default). apaginate runs the count and the page as two statements; concurrent writes can make total and items disagree slightly. @db.ordered_by applies only when a query has no order_by . Counts and bulk updates ignore it. Reusable queries ¶ A reusable query is a typed class method returning a QuerySet . There is no hidden default manager: Model.all() always means every row. # notes/apps/billing/models.py (continued) from typing import Self from hinoki.orm import QuerySet class Invoice ( Model ): ... # fields as in Define models voided_at : datetime | None = None @classmethod def open ( cls ) -> QuerySet [ Self ]: return cls . filter ( voided_at = None , paid = False ) Pass it where the framework asks for a base query, so every operation sees the same rows: # notes/apps/billing/api.py from typing import Any from hinoki import API , Caller , crud from hinoki.admin import ModelAdmin from hinoki.orm import QuerySet from notes.security import billing_staff from .models import Invoice from .schemas import InvoiceOut @crud ( Invoice , path = "/invoices" , read = InvoiceOut , access = billing_staff ) class Invoices ( API ): def get_queryset ( self , principal : Caller [ Any ] | None ) -> QuerySet [ Invoice ]: return Invoice . open () class InvoiceAdmin ( ModelAdmin [ Invoice ]): def queryset ( self , principal : Caller [ Any ]) -> QuerySet [ Invoice ]: return Invoice . open () Rule Where row order @db.ordered_by(...) ( model options ) an app-wide policy, such as hiding voided rows a named class method, used in get_queryset() and ModelAdmin.queryset() rows that depend on the caller get_queryset(principal) or ModelAdmin.queryset(principal) Not a security boundary Model.all() and raw SQL skip a reusable query. Keep ownership and permissions in access= , owner= and ModelAdmin.can() . Create and update ¶ # inside an async operation invoice = await Invoice . acreate ( InvoiceIn ( reference = "INV-8" ), customer_id = customer . id ) invoice . paid = True await invoice . asave () # updates the changed columns await invoice . aupdate_from ( InvoicePatch ( paid = False )) changed = await Invoice . aupdate_where ({ "id" : invoice . id , "paid" : False }, { "paid" : True }) Keywords set by the server win over values from a Schema ; a Schema never carries the primary key. asave() writes changed columns and refuses a primary-key change. aupdate_where(conditions, values) puts ownership and state checks in the SQL condition: use it for conditional writes instead of read-then-write. QuerySet.aupdate(values) and adelete() act on every matching row, ignore ordering and refuse a query with limit or offset ; select the keys first and filter on id__in=[...] . Writing many rows at once ¶ abulk_create , abulk_update and abulk_delete (sync bulk_* ) each run in one transaction, or a savepoint inside an open one: # inside an async operation rows = await Invoice . abulk_create ( [ { "reference" : "A-1" , "customer_id" : customer . id }, { "reference" : "A-2" , "customer_id" : customer . id }, ] ) rows [ 0 ] . paid = True await Invoice . abulk_update ( rows ) # saves changed rows only deleted = await Invoice . abulk_delete ([ rows [ 0 ], rows [ 1 ] . id ]) # instances or keys abulk_create takes Schema objects or dicts, each carrying every required value, and returns the rows in order; defaults, factories, validation and hooks apply as for acreate . It takes no server keywords: put them in each item. abulk_update refuses an unsaved instance and returns every instance it was given, unchanged ones included; abulk_delete returns how many rows existed, deletes in chunks of at most 10 000 keys and runs no hooks. One statement per row (per chunk for deletes): these give atomicity, not a batching speed-up. Writes that do not read the row back ¶ By default a write returns the stored row ( RETURNING on PostgreSQL and SQLite, a follow-up SELECT in the same transaction on MySQL and MariaDB). returning=False skips that: # inside an async operation draft = await Invoice . acreate ( reference = "D-1" , customer_id = customer . id , returning = False ) count = await Invoice . aupdate ( id = draft . id , paid = True , returning = False ) count = await Invoice . filter ( customer_id = customer . id ) . aupdate ( { "paid" : False }, returning = False ) Method Default returning=False acreate , insert the stored row the same instance, holding the sent values aupdate the stored row; NotFound when nothing matches int row count; 0 , no NotFound aupdate_where , QuerySet.aupdate list of stored rows int row count Nothing is re-read: database-side changes (timestamp precision, numeric scale, JSON normalization, triggers) are not reflected; read with aget when you need them. @db.timestamps() and validation still run. PostgreSQL and SQLite count matched rows; MySQL and MariaDB count rows whose values changed. A model cannot declare a field named returning . See also ¶ Relations : select_related and prefetch_related Lifecycle hooks Transactions Typing : what type checkers see for keyword-based methods

docs.text: Async Sync # inside an async operation or handler invoice = await Invoice . aget ( id = invoice_id ) maybe = await Invoice . aget_or_none ( reference = "INV-7" ) unpaid = await Invoice . filter ( customer_id = customer . id , paid = False ) . order_by ( "reference" ) first = await Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . afirst () count = await Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . acount () page = await Invoice . all () . apaginate ( PageParams ( page = 1 , page_size = 20 )) # inside a sync handler (runs in the bounded worker pool) invoice = Invoice . get ( id = invoice_id ) maybe = Invoice . get_or_none ( reference = "INV-7" ) unpaid = ( Invoice . filter ( customer_id = customer . id , paid = False ) . order_by ( "reference" ) . list () ) first = Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . first () count = Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . count () page = Invoice . all () . paginate ( PageParams ( page = 1 , page_size = 20 )) PageParams comes from hinoki.pagination . aget raises Invoice.NotFound (a 404 in a request) or MultipleObjectsReturned . Building a query ( filter , order_by , limit , offset , select_related ) issues no SQL; awaiting it or calling an evaluation method does.
docs.title: Query rows

docs.text: filter(field=value) and filter(field__op=value) accept model field names and the supported comparison and membership operators ( ne , in , isnull , gt , gte , lt , lte , contains ). SQL identifiers come from model metadata. field__ne=value compiles to <> : rows where the column is NULL are not returned. Add an isnull filter when they matter. contains matches text case-insensitively and treats % , _ and \ literally. SQLite folds ASCII case only; MySQL and MariaDB assume the NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES mode is off (the default). apaginate runs the count and the page as two statements; concurrent writes can make total and items disagree slightly. @db.ordered_by applies only when a query has no order_by . Counts and bulk updates ignore it.
docs.title: Filters

docs.text: A reusable query is a typed class method returning a QuerySet . There is no hidden default manager: Model.all() always means every row. # notes/apps/billing/models.py (continued) from typing import Self from hinoki.orm import QuerySet class Invoice ( Model ): ... # fields as in Define models voided_at : datetime | None = None @classmethod def open ( cls ) -> QuerySet [ Self ]: return cls . filter ( voided_at = None , paid = False ) Pass it where the framework asks for a base query, so every operation sees the same rows: # notes/apps/billing/api.py from typing import Any from hinoki import API , Caller , crud from hinoki.admin import ModelAdmin from hinoki.orm import QuerySet from notes.security import billing_staff from .models import Invoice from .schemas import InvoiceOut @crud ( Invoice , path = "/invoices" , read = InvoiceOut , access = billing_staff ) class Invoices ( API ): def get_queryset ( self , principal : Caller [ Any ] | None ) -> QuerySet [ Invoice ]: return Invoice . open () class InvoiceAdmin ( ModelAdmin [ Invoice ]): def queryset ( self , principal : Caller [ Any ]) -> QuerySet [ Invoice ]: return Invoice . open () Rule Where row order @db.ordered_by(...) ( model options ) an app-wide policy, such as hiding voided rows a named class method, used in get_queryset() and ModelAdmin.queryset() rows that depend on the caller get_queryset(principal) or ModelAdmin.queryset(principal) Not a security boundary Model.all() and raw SQL skip a reusable query. Keep ownership and permissions in access= , owner= and ModelAdmin.can() .
docs.title: Reusable queries

docs.text: # inside an async operation invoice = await Invoice . acreate ( InvoiceIn ( reference = "INV-8" ), customer_id = customer . id ) invoice . paid = True await invoice . asave () # updates the changed columns await invoice . aupdate_from ( InvoicePatch ( paid = False )) changed = await Invoice . aupdate_where ({ "id" : invoice . id , "paid" : False }, { "paid" : True }) Keywords set by the server win over values from a Schema ; a Schema never carries the primary key. asave() writes changed columns and refuses a primary-key change. aupdate_where(conditions, values) puts ownership and state checks in the SQL condition: use it for conditional writes instead of read-then-write. QuerySet.aupdate(values) and adelete() act on every matching row, ignore ordering and refuse a query with limit or offset ; select the keys first and filter on id__in=[...] .
docs.title: Create and update

docs.text: abulk_create , abulk_update and abulk_delete (sync bulk_* ) each run in one transaction, or a savepoint inside an open one: # inside an async operation rows = await Invoice . abulk_create ( [ { "reference" : "A-1" , "customer_id" : customer . id }, { "reference" : "A-2" , "customer_id" : customer . id }, ] ) rows [ 0 ] . paid = True await Invoice . abulk_update ( rows ) # saves changed rows only deleted = await Invoice . abulk_delete ([ rows [ 0 ], rows [ 1 ] . id ]) # instances or keys abulk_create takes Schema objects or dicts, each carrying every required value, and returns the rows in order; defaults, factories, validation and hooks apply as for acreate . It takes no server keywords: put them in each item. abulk_update refuses an unsaved instance and returns every instance it was given, unchanged ones included; abulk_delete returns how many rows existed, deletes in chunks of at most 10 000 keys and runs no hooks. One statement per row (per chunk for deletes): these give atomicity, not a batching speed-up.
docs.title: Writing many rows at once

docs.text: By default a write returns the stored row ( RETURNING on PostgreSQL and SQLite, a follow-up SELECT in the same transaction on MySQL and MariaDB). returning=False skips that: # inside an async operation draft = await Invoice . acreate ( reference = "D-1" , customer_id = customer . id , returning = False ) count = await Invoice . aupdate ( id = draft . id , paid = True , returning = False ) count = await Invoice . filter ( customer_id = customer . id ) . aupdate ( { "paid" : False }, returning = False ) Method Default returning=False acreate , insert the stored row the same instance, holding the sent values aupdate the stored row; NotFound when nothing matches int row count; 0 , no NotFound aupdate_where , QuerySet.aupdate list of stored rows int row count Nothing is re-read: database-side changes (timestamp precision, numeric scale, JSON normalization, triggers) are not reflected; read with aget when you need them. @db.timestamps() and validation still run. PostgreSQL and SQLite count matched rows; MySQL and MariaDB count rows whose values changed. A model cannot declare a field named returning .
docs.title: Writes that do not read the row back

docs.text: Quick start ¶ Create a project, run its tests and serve it. Everything runs locally; the database is a SQLite file. Create a project ¶ From the Hinoki checkout: uv run hinoki new hinoki new asks only what it needs. Give these answers and keep the other defaults: Prompt Default Answer Project name notes Parent directory . .. (beside the checkout) Database none sqlite Server kiso kiso Agent instructions and MCP config? yes yes Agent skills? no no Initialize a git repository? yes yes Install dependencies (uv sync)? yes yes Create an app now? yes yes App name core entries It writes the project and the entries app, runs git init and uv sync , and prints the next commands. The files that matter: notes/ ├── hinoki.toml manifest: application, routes and the entries app ├── notes/ │ ├── main.py the application │ ├── api.py GET /health │ ├── routes.py routes = [health] │ ├── settings.py typed settings, NOTES_* variables │ ├── rules.py architecture rules │ └── apps/entries/ models, endpoints, routes and migrations of the app ├── tests/ pytest suite └── AGENTS.md agent instructions The project package holds no models. They live in apps; answering no to the last question leaves the project without one, and Add another app shows how to add it later. Scripts and CI uv run hinoki new notes --dir .. --no-input --database sqlite --git --install --app entries gives the same answers without prompts. Plain --no-input uses the defaults instead: no database, no git init , no uv sync and no app. All options are in hinoki new . Test and serve it ¶ cd ../notes uv run pytest uv run hinoki dev The test calls /health in process and needs no database. hinoki dev serves on http://127.0.0.1:8000 and reloads when a file changes. In another terminal: curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health {"status":"ok"} At startup hinoki dev logs a warning that allowed_hosts is '*' : the application answers to any Host header. It is harmless on your machine. To name the hosts you serve, and silence it, add NOTES_ALLOWED_HOSTS=127.0.0.1,localhost to .env ; see allowed_hosts . Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs for the generated OpenAPI UI, or run uv run hinoki routes to list every route with its access policy. What the manifest does ¶ hinoki.toml names the application and where its routes live; each app you create adds its own models, migrations and routes: [project] application = "notes.main:app" routes = "notes.routes:routes" notes/main.py declares the application: # notes/main.py from hinoki import Hinoki from hinoki.project import manifest_routes from notes.rules import project_rules from notes.settings import ProjectSettings app = Hinoki ( settings = ProjectSettings , # NOTES_* variables and .env include = manifest_routes (), # notes/routes.py, then each app's routes at its prefix title = "Notes" , openapi_url = "/openapi.json" , docs_url = "/docs" , rules = project_rules , ) manifest_routes() reads hinoki.toml , so the application lists no routes of its own. Commands read the same file, so inside the project they need no module paths. Where the database is configured ¶ Answering sqlite added one field to notes/settings.py : # notes/settings.py from hinoki import settings class ProjectSettings ( settings . AppSettings , prefix = "NOTES_" , dotenv = ".env" ): database : settings . DatabaseSettings With no value set, it is the SQLite file .hinoki/local.sqlite3 . Each field of DatabaseSettings is a NOTES_DATABASE__<FIELD> variable (two underscores between the group and the field), read from the environment or from .env in the project directory. uv run hinoki settings lists every variable and where its value came from. To use another file: # .env NOTES_DATABASE__URL = sqlite://./.hinoki/notes.sqlite3 Configure a database covers PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, and connection fields instead of a URL. The project has no models yet; add them in the app, as the next section and the tutorial show. Your first app ¶ Models live in apps, not in the project package. hinoki new created entries when you answered the last question: notes/apps/entries/ ├── api.py endpoints of the app ├── routes.py the routes served, mounted at /entries ├── models.py tables of the app └── migrations/ migration history It is registered in hinoki.toml : [[apps]] name = "entries" models = "notes.apps.entries.models" migrations = "notes.apps.entries.migrations" routes = "notes.apps.entries.routes:routes" prefix = "/entries" requires = [] App names are lower-case letters and digits with single underscores between words (for example api_v1 ), starting with a letter. Define the app's models in notes/apps/entries/models.py , then uv run hinoki migrations plan entries ; 8. Projects and apps walks through it. Add another app ¶ If you answered no, or want a second app, create it from the project: uv run hinoki app create billing Next ¶ Tutorial : build an API layer by layer. 8. Projects and apps : add an app with its own models and migrations to this project. Notes example : a small CRUD API whose model lives in notes/apps/notes .

docs.text: Relations ¶ A relation is an ordinary foreign-key column. Related rows load only when a query asks for them: attribute access never performs I/O. Declare a foreign key ¶ # notes/apps/billing/models.py from typing import ClassVar from uuid import UUID , uuid4 from hinoki import db from hinoki.orm import Model , OnDelete , Related , field , foreign_key , pk class Customer ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) name : str = field ( max_length = 120 ) invoices : ClassVar [ "Related[list[Invoice]]" ] @db . indexed ( "customer_id" ) class Invoice ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) customer_id : UUID = foreign_key ( Customer , on_delete = OnDelete . RESTRICT , related_name = "invoices" ) reference : str = field ( max_length = 40 , unique = True ) customer : ClassVar [ Related [ Customer ]] customer_id is stored on billing_invoices . invoice.customer is the forward relation (named after the column without _id ); customer.invoices is the reverse relation, created only when related_name is set. The ClassVar[Related[...]] lines are for type checkers. The column type must match the referenced primary key. on_delete is required and takes an OnDelete member: on_delete When the referenced row is deleted OnDelete.RESTRICT the delete is refused while references exist OnDelete.CASCADE referencing rows are deleted too OnDelete.SET_NULL the column becomes NULL ; the field must be \| None OnDelete.NO_ACTION like RESTRICT , checked at the end of the statement A refused delete raises hinoki.db.DatabaseError ( database request failed ), not UniqueViolation , so it is not translated to 409 : check for references first, or register an error handler for it. Text such as on_delete="cascade" , and SET_NULL on a non-nullable field, are refused with RegistrationError at import: # notes/apps/billing/models.py (continued) @db . indexed ( "invoice_id" ) class Payment ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) invoice_id : UUID | None = foreign_key ( Invoice , on_delete = OnDelete . SET_NULL , default = None ) The rule becomes the migration's REFERENCES … ON DELETE clause and the database enforces it. Load related rows ¶ # inside an async operation invoices = await Invoice . all () . select_related ( "customer" ) names = [ invoice . customer . name for invoice in invoices ] customers = await Customer . all () . prefetch_related ( "invoices" ) counts = { c . id : len ( c . invoices ) for c in customers } Method Use for SQL select_related("customer") a forward foreign key (one row) one LEFT JOIN in the same statement prefetch_related("invoices") a reverse or collection relation one separate, bounded query Reading a relation that was not loaded raises RelationNotLoaded . acount() and apaginate() drop a select_related join from their COUNT (a to-one join cannot change the count) but keep a join a filter needs, such as customer__name=... . One-to-one ¶ A one-to-one relation is a foreign key with unique=True : # notes/apps/billing/models.py (continued) class BillingProfile ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) customer_id : UUID = foreign_key ( Customer , on_delete = OnDelete . CASCADE , unique = True , related_name = "profile" ) vat_number : str = field ( max_length = 20 ) customer : ClassVar [ Related [ Customer ]] Add profile: ClassVar["Related[BillingProfile | None]"] to Customer for type checkers. profile.customer has one required target; customer.profile is BillingProfile | None . Load them with select_related("customer") and prefetch_related("profile") . If the database has drifted and holds several rows for one customer, prefetch_related raises MultipleObjectsReturned . The migration creates the foreign key and the unique constraint together. It fails on existing duplicates; clean them up first. Turning an existing foreign key into unique=True rebuilds the table on SQLite and needs a hand-written migration on PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB. Many-to-many ¶ There is no implicit join table or through= : declare the association model. # notes/apps/billing/models.py (continued) class Tag ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) name : str = field ( max_length = 40 , unique = True ) invoice_links : ClassVar [ "Related[list[InvoiceTag]]" ] @db . unique ( "invoice_id" , "tag_id" ) @db . indexed ( "tag_id" ) class InvoiceTag ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) invoice_id : UUID = foreign_key ( Invoice , on_delete = OnDelete . CASCADE , related_name = "tag_links" ) tag_id : UUID = foreign_key ( Tag , on_delete = OnDelete . CASCADE , related_name = "invoice_links" ) The composite unique constraint stops duplicate pairs and indexes invoice_id ; @db.indexed("tag_id") indexes the other side. Link and read: # inside an async operation tag = await Tag . acreate ( name = "priority" ) await InvoiceTag . acreate ( invoice_id = invoice . id , tag_id = tag . id ) links = await InvoiceTag . filter ( invoice_id = invoice . id ) . select_related ( "tag" ) tag_names = [ link . tag . name for link in links ] invoice.tag_links holds InvoiceTag rows (load it with prefetch_related("tag_links") ), not Tag objects. The association model can carry its own columns, such as when the tag was added. Foreign keys in abstract models and mixins ¶ A foreign key in an abstract model or mixin is registered once per table model that inherits it. Give the reverse relation a per-model name with the {model} placeholder (the class name in lower case): # notes/apps/billing/models.py (continued) class CustomerOwned ( Model , abstract = True ): customer_id : UUID = foreign_key ( Customer , on_delete = OnDelete . CASCADE , related_name = " {model} _set" ) class CreditNote ( CustomerOwned ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) class Estimate ( CustomerOwned ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) Customer gets creditnote_set and estimate_set . A fixed related_name makes the second inheriting model fail with an error naming both. Without related_name there is no reverse relation. A foreign key cannot reference an abstract model. {model} is the only placeholder. See also ¶ Query and write rows Migrations : foreign-key changes and backend notes

docs.text: Request lifecycle ¶ The order matters: validation, access and transactions fail in different ways and at different moments. Accept. Kiso accepts the connection, answers what needs no application code and hands the rest to the request pipeline ( Kiso ). With --server granian , Granian calls the ASGI application, which reaches the same pipeline. Route. Hinoki matches the method and path. Authenticate and authorize. For an action with an access policy, the provider resolves a Caller and the policy checks permissions. A rate_limit= policy runs next. The body has not been read yet, so an unauthenticated or rate-limited client cannot make the server buffer it. Bind. Hinoki negotiates the response type from Accept ( 406 when nothing fits), reads the body of POST , PUT , PATCH and QUERY requests, then binds and validates path, query, header and body values. Open the transaction for an atomic=True action. Run the handler , then check its value against the return annotation (a mismatch is 500 internal_error , inside the transaction, unless the action sets validate_response=False ) and render it. A returned Response is neither checked nor rendered. Commit after the response is prepared. An exception or cancellation rolls back before the HTTP error is produced. An unhandled exception never becomes a successful response, and a failed commit is an error. A renderer must not perform hidden database I/O. Limits ¶ Setting Default When exceeded execution.request_timeout 30 s, through response preparation 504 timeout ; an open transaction rolls back execution.max_body_bytes 1 MiB (also each multipart part) 413 payload_too_large execution.max_query_bytes 8 KiB 414 uri_too_long execution.max_header_bytes 32 KiB, names and values combined 431 headers_too_large The size checks run before routing. A sync handler already running when the timeout expires cannot be stopped: it keeps its executor slot until it returns, and its result is discarded. Let the proxy or ASGI server enforce its own request-line and header limits too. Request IDs ¶ Each response carries a request ID in server.request_id_header ( x-request-id ), and built-in error JSON repeats it as request_id . Hinoki generates it; with server.trust_request_id=True it accepts a validated inbound ID, only from a trusted proxy. Startup and shutdown ¶ lifecycle.startup_timeout (30 s) and lifecycle.shutdown_timeout (10 s) bound the worker lifespan. A startup failure is reported through the ASGI lifespan protocol; shutdown cleans up resources within its deadline. Startup and shutdown hooks run inside those limits. Where Rust runs ¶ Routing, parsing, validation and selected serialization run in Rust; the server hand-off (Granian and the ASGI adapter, or Kiso's queue) crosses Python objects. See sync and async code for which executor runs what. See also ¶ Transactions Errors Serving

docs.text: The order matters: validation, access and transactions fail in different ways and at different moments. Accept. Kiso accepts the connection, answers what needs no application code and hands the rest to the request pipeline ( Kiso ). With --server granian , Granian calls the ASGI application, which reaches the same pipeline. Route. Hinoki matches the method and path. Authenticate and authorize. For an action with an access policy, the provider resolves a Caller and the policy checks permissions. A rate_limit= policy runs next. The body has not been read yet, so an unauthenticated or rate-limited client cannot make the server buffer it. Bind. Hinoki negotiates the response type from Accept ( 406 when nothing fits), reads the body of POST , PUT , PATCH and QUERY requests, then binds and validates path, query, header and body values. Open the transaction for an atomic=True action. Run the handler , then check its value against the return annotation (a mismatch is 500 internal_error , inside the transaction, unless the action sets validate_response=False ) and render it. A returned Response is neither checked nor rendered. Commit after the response is prepared. An exception or cancellation rolls back before the HTTP error is produced. An unhandled exception never becomes a successful response, and a failed commit is an error. A renderer must not perform hidden database I/O.

docs.text: Register routes ¶ An application serves the routes that hinoki.toml points to. The project and each app keep their routes in a routes.py that exports a list, and notes/main.py includes them all with manifest_routes() . From the manifest to the application ¶ # hinoki.toml [project] application = "notes.main:app" routes = "notes.routes:routes" # the project's own routes [[apps]] name = "billing" models = "notes.apps.billing.models" migrations = "notes.apps.billing.migrations" routes = "notes.apps.billing.routes:routes" prefix = "/billing" # "/<name>" when omitted requires = [] # notes/main.py from hinoki import Hinoki from hinoki.project import manifest_routes from notes.rules import project_rules from notes.settings import ProjectSettings app = Hinoki ( settings = ProjectSettings , include = manifest_routes (), title = "Notes" , openapi_url = "/openapi.json" , docs_url = "/docs" , rules = project_rules , ) manifest_routes() finds hinoki.toml from the calling file's directory upwards and returns, in order: the project's routes list, at its own paths; each app's routes list under the app's prefix , apps in dependency order ( requires ). An app without a routes key, or with an empty list, adds nothing. Outside a project it raises ProjectError . hinoki app create billing writes the routes.py and the manifest keys; hinoki app create billing --prefix /payments chooses another prefix. hinoki app list prints each app with its routes and prefix. One place for each prefix ¶ Segment Declared by Example The app prefix in hinoki.toml /billing A version inside the app Mount in routes.py /v2 The resource RouteGroup(...) or API, path=... /invoices Write each segment once. Paths in code are relative to the app, so moving an app is a one-line change in hinoki.toml . Versions with Mount ¶ Mount(prefix, *items) prepends its prefix to everything it holds. Use it inside routes.py when one app serves several versions: # notes/apps/billing/routes.py from hinoki import Includable , Mount from . import v1 , v2 routes : list [ Includable ] = [ Mount ( "/v1" , v1 . routes ), Mount ( "/v2" , v2 . routes ), ] The result is /billing/v1/invoices and /billing/v2/invoices . Mounts nest, and their prefixes join from the outside in. A prefix starts with / and does not end with one, and a mount holds at least one item. Mounting changes the path only: access, errors and transactions stay as declared. What include accepts ¶ Includable is the type of every item a routes list may hold: Item Example A decorated function health A RouteGroup invoices An API class, including a @crud class Invoices A crud(...) value crud(Invoice, path="/invoices", read=InvoiceOut) A Mount Mount("/v1", v1.routes) An object with an api() method the admin A list or tuple of these v1.routes Nested lists are spread in place, in the order you wrote them. Annotate each list as routes: list[Includable] so the type checker rejects anything else; a module passed instead of its list is refused with a hint to export a list. The application module ¶ Declare app once, at module level, in the module that project.application names. Importing it reads the settings and builds declarations; nothing connects until a worker starts, so commands, servers and tests import the same object. A factory target ( module:create_app ) is still accepted by the commands, for code that must build the application from runtime values. Routes for tests and options ¶ To serve a subset, or the same routes with other settings, build another Hinoki with an explicit include= : # tests/billingroutestest.py from hinoki import Hinoki , Mount from notes.apps.billing.routes import routes app = Hinoki ( include = [ Mount ( "/billing" , routes )]) include=[] is an empty application. To add routes that exist only when a setting is on, call app.include(...) in the application module before it serves: # notes/main.py (continued) from hinoki import Mount from notes.apps.billing.exports import exports if app . settings . billing_exports : app . include ( Mount ( "/billing" , exports )) Inspect the map ¶ hinoki routes hinoki routes --path /billing --method POST hinoki routes --format json Rows are sorted by path, then method, and show the effective access policy and the handler. --lanes adds the serving lane of each route. See list routes with routes for every option. Errors and edge cases ¶ Everything below fails when the application is built, before it serves a request: Message Cause cannot load the routes of app 'billing' (notes.apps.billing.routes:routes): … The module or attribute in hinoki.toml does not import the routes of app 'billing' (…) must be a list of routes routes is a single item, not a list or tuple RegistrationError naming an action Two routes reach the same method and path after prefixes join RegistrationError: application is already serving; it is frozen app.include(...) after the server started An include call registers all its items or none of them.

docs.text: Check architecture with rules ¶ Rules are typed promises about your application: "every private action names a policy", "writes are atomic", "no response leaks password_hash ". Each one is a Python object with a stable ID, deterministic behaviour and an exact fix line. They are optional, and a project created with hinoki new starts with them on: # notes/rules.py """The project's rules. Weaken them only with the owner's decision (see hinoki-rules.toml).""" from hinoki import Actions , Schemas , Transactions # add Models with your first model from hinoki.rules import RuleSet project_rules = RuleSet ( # Anything not public on purpose names an access policy, and the policy names permissions. Actions . require_access ( match = "notes.*" , except_ = [ "notes.api.health" ]), Actions . require_permissions ( match = "notes.*" , except_ = [ "notes.api.health" ]), # Responses are concrete Schema types and lists are paginated. Actions . forbid_model_responses ( match = "notes.*" ), Actions . require_return_type ( match = "notes.*" ), Actions . require_pagination ( match = "notes.*" ), # Writes run in a transaction that rolls back before errors become HTTP. Transactions . require_atomic (), # Secrets never reach a client, and request text is bounded. Schemas . forbid_exposure ( "password_hash" , "password" , "token" ), Schemas . require_string_limits (), # Turn these on with your first model (a model rule that matches no model # fails the check): tables are pinned and foreign keys are indexed. # Models.require_explicit_table(match="notes.*"), # Models.require_foreign_key_index(match="notes.*"), ) notes/main.py passes the set to the application with rules=project_rules . Check it at any time: hinoki check The eleven rules ¶ ID Rule Phase Checks HNK-ACC-001 Actions.require_access(match="*", except_=()) startup every matching action names an Access policy (public by default is the common hole) HNK-ACC-002 Actions.require_permissions(match="*", except_=()) startup an action with an Access policy names at least one permission, so "any authenticated caller" is never implicit HNK-API-001 Actions.forbid_model_responses(match="*", except_=()) startup no action returns a Model (or a list or page of them): responses are Schema classes HNK-API-002 Actions.require_return_type(match="*", except_=()) startup every action annotates a concrete return type (not missing, Any or object ; None is fine for a 204 ) HNK-API-003 Actions.require_pagination(match="*", except_=()) startup a GET action never returns a plain list[...] (alone or in a union): it returns a Page HNK-TXN-001 Transactions.require_atomic(methods=("POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"), match="*", except_=()) startup state-changing actions declare atomic=True , on the action or its RouteGroup HNK-SCH-001 Schemas.forbid_exposure(*fields) startup the named fields never appear in a response Schema : nested, in a subclass, in a union variant, as a field, an alias or a computed field HNK-SCH-002 Schemas.require_string_limits() startup every text field a client sends (nested, in containers, dict values and union variants included) has max_length or one_of ; Enum and Literal fields pass HNK-DB-001 Models.require_explicit_table(match="*") startup matching models pin their table with @db.table(...) or table= , so renaming the class cannot rename the table HNK-DB-002 Models.require_foreign_key_index(match="*") startup every foreign-key column leads an index, a primary key or a unique constraint HNK-IMP-001 Imports.forbid(source, target) static modules under source never import target , read from the source files; dynamic imports are reported, not ignored Every built-in rule has severity error . HNK-API-002 matters most for actions with validate_response=False : any other action with an unusable return annotation already stops the app. HNK-TXN-001 does not check the admin's own routes, which open their own short transactions. Choose what a rule covers ¶ Action rules match fnmatch patterns against an action's qualified name: module.function for a function, module.Class.method for an API class (named after the class it is mounted on), and module.<Model>Crud.<action> for a crud(...) value, where module is the one that calls crud(...) . A bare health matches nothing; write notes.api.health or *.health . except_ takes the same patterns and is how you say "public on purpose". The Blog example names its exceptions once: # blog/rules.py PUBLIC = [ "blog.api.health" , "blog.api.Posts.listing" , "blog.api.Posts.one" , "blog.accounts.*.login" , # public on purpose: it is how you sign in ] SIGNED_IN = [ "blog.accounts.*.me" ] # any signed-in user, no permission blog_rules = RuleSet ( Actions . require_access ( match = "blog.*" , except_ = PUBLIC ), Actions . require_permissions ( match = "blog.*" , except_ = [ * PUBLIC , * SIGNED_IN ]), Transactions . require_atomic ( except_ = [ "blog.accounts.*.login" ]), Schemas . forbid_exposure ( "token" , "password_hash" ), Imports . forbid ( source = "blog.models" , target = "blog.api" ), # ... and the other six rules, see examples/blog/rules.py ) The model rules match the model's module ( blog.* ) and report unverifiable when no model matches, even with * . In a project with hinoki.toml , hinoki check first imports the models of every [[apps]] entry, so they are found without importing them from the application module. require_access and require_atomic report unverifiable when a pattern other than * matches no action. Neither passes silently. When rules run ¶ Where Rules Waivers On failure Application startup ( hinoki dev , hinoki serve , any ASGI server, the test clients) startup rules of rules= the waiver file startup fails with RegistrationError listing every failing diagnostic hinoki check both phases (or --phase ) the waiver file, or --waivers exit code 1 hinoki mcp both phases the waiver file, or --waivers reported to the agent Startup enforcement means a broken promise never serves traffic. During a migration you can pass enforce_rules=False to Hinoki(...) : violations are then logged as a warning instead. Read the results ¶ hinoki check prints one line per finding, with its location and a fix: hint. This output comes from a deliberately broken project in Hinoki's own tests, checked from a clone of the repository: hinoki check tests.projects.rulesapp:create_app --rules tests.projects.rulesapp:rules tests/projects/rulesapp.py:7: HNK-ACC-001 [violated] GET /health (health) declares no access policy fix: add access=<policy> to the action (or list it in except_ when it is public on purpose) tests/projects/rulesapp.py:12: HNK-ACC-001 [violated] POST /items (create) declares no access policy fix: add access=<policy> to the action (or list it in except_ when it is public on purpose) tests/projects/rulesapp.py:12: HNK-TXN-001 [violated] POST /items (create) does not declare atomic=True fix: add atomic=True to the action (or declare it on a RouteGroup(..., atomic=True) group) 2 rule(s): 3 violated, 0 unverifiable, 0 waived Each status means one thing: violated (demonstrated), unverifiable (the check could not decide: a dynamic import, a pattern that matched nothing, a return type that does not name its schema, or a rule that crashed), waived and warning (a notice about the waiver file itself). Unverifiable fails like a violation; it is never a pass. A warning never fails. The fix line each rule prints: ID fix: HNK-ACC-002 name at least one permission in the Access policy of the action HNK-API-001 return a Schema (for example PostOut.from_model(row)) instead of the Model HNK-API-002 annotate the action's return type (a Schema, or None for status 204) HNK-API-003 return Page[Item] and paginate the action instead of returning a list HNK-SCH-001 remove the field from the response Schema, or return a Schema that does not carry it HNK-SCH-002 bound the field: Annotated[str, Field(max_length=...)] or one_of=... HNK-DB-001 name the table with @db.table(...) or table=... on the model HNK-DB-002 index the column: @db.indexed(" ") on the model, or an index or unique group that starts with it HNK-IMP-001 move the code to an allowed layer, or depend on it through the layer in between hinoki check --format json prints the same diagnostics as versioned data ( schema_version , rules , summary , and per diagnostic rule , severity , phase , status , message , location , explanation , subject , waiver , fix ) for CI, editors and agents. summary counts each status ( violated , unverifiable , waived , warning ) and adds failing , the number that sets the exit code. schema_version is 2 : version 1 reported waiver notices as violated and had no warning count. Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 failing, 2 the check could not run. The other options are on Inspect an application . Accept an exception with a waiver ¶ Prefer except_ for things that are public or special by design . A waiver is for a known violation the owner accepts for a while. It lives in hinoki-rules.toml at the project root, which hinoki new creates: # hinoki-rules.toml [[waiver]] rule = "HNK-ACC-001" target = "tests.projects.rulesapp.health" reason = "liveness probe is public by design" owner = "platform-team" expires = 2027-01-31 rule , target , reason and owner are required. target is an fnmatch pattern on the diagnostic's subject and must be bounded: a literal prefix of at least five characters containing a dot ( shop.api.* , never * ). expires is optional and must be a TOML date, written without quotes; the waiver applies through that day and expires once the current UTC date is later. The waived diagnostic keeps its line and gains the decision: tests/projects/rulesapp.py:7: HNK-ACC-001 [waived] GET /health (health) declares no access policy fix: add access=<policy> to the action (or list it in except_ when it is public on purpose) waived: liveness probe is public by design (platform-team, until 2027-01-31) An expired waiver stops applying and reports HNK-WVR-002 ; one that matches nothing reports HNK-WVR-001 . Both have status warning : they print as [warning] , count under warning(s) in the summary ( summary.warning in JSON) and never change the exit code. A diagnostic that means "the rule could not do its job" cannot be waived. An invalid or unreadable file makes hinoki check exit with 2 . Which waiver file ¶ hinoki check , hinoki mcp and application startup read the same file: The file named by Hinoki(waivers=...) , or by --waivers on check and mcp . A named file must exist. Otherwise hinoki-rules.toml at the project root: the directory of the nearest hinoki.toml , searched from the working directory upwards. Running from a subdirectory of the project finds the same file. Without a hinoki.toml , hinoki-rules.toml in the working directory. app = Hinoki ( rules = rules , waivers = "config/hinoki-rules.toml" ) A missing default file means no waivers. A directory or a broken symbolic link with that name is an error, not an absent file. hinoki mcp --waivers PATH also applies PATH to the app that run_scenario starts. Waivers at startup ¶ Application startup applies the waiver file the same way as hinoki check . This app requires access on every action, yet it starts and serves /health because the owner waived it: # shop/main.py from hinoki import Actions , Hinoki , Request , http from hinoki.rules import RuleSet @http . get ( "/health" ) def health ( request : Request ) -> dict [ str , str ]: return { "status" : "ok" } app = Hinoki ( rules = RuleSet ( Actions . require_access ()), include = [ health ]) # hinoki-rules.toml [[waiver]] rule = "HNK-ACC-001" target = "shop.main.health" reason = "liveness probe is public by design" owner = "platform-team" Without the waiver, hinoki serve fails at startup with RegistrationError: 1 rule violation(s) . At startup: An absent default file means no waivers. An invalid or unreadable file, or a missing file named with waivers= , fails startup with RegistrationError ("invalid waivers: .../hinoki-rules.toml: waiver #1: missing target"), even with enforce_rules=False . An expired waiver does not apply: the violation fails startup and the RegistrationError also lists the HNK-WVR-002 notice. Without a remaining violation the notice is logged as a warning. HNK-WVR-001 (unused waiver) is reported only by hinoki check and hinoki mcp : startup runs only the startup rules, so a waiver for a static rule such as HNK-IMP-001 is expected to match nothing there. Waivers are the owner's decision: tools read the file and never write it. Put it under CODEOWNERS; the generated AGENTS.md tells agents the same. Your own rules ¶ Subclass hinoki.rules.Rule with a stable id , an explanation , an optional fix and a check that yields diagnostics. phase defaults to Phase.STARTUP and severity to Severity.ERROR . # notes/rules.py from collections.abc import Iterator from hinoki.rules import Diagnostic , Project , Rule , qualified , where class NoDelete ( Rule ): id = "NOTES-API-001" explanation = "This project archives rows instead of deleting them." fix = "use PATCH to set archived=true" def check ( self , project : Project ) -> Iterator [ Diagnostic ]: for route in project . app . routes : if route . method == "DELETE" : yield self . diagnostic ( f "DELETE { route . path } removes a row" , where ( route . handler ), subject = qualified ( route ), ) Add NoDelete() to the RuleSet . where(obj) gives a file:line location; qualified(route) gives the subject that waivers match (without a subject the location is used; an empty subject cannot be waived). A rule that needs side effects (running code, files, network, a database) lists them in effects and only runs under hinoki check --allow-effects ; at startup it is refused and reported as unverifiable. RuleSet raises ValueError for an empty ID or the same ID twice. Errors and edge cases ¶ A rule that raises is reported as unverifiable with "the rule failed to run", never skipped. HNK-IMP-001 runs only in hinoki check and hinoki mcp ; it needs the source files of the checked packages ( --package , default: the target's top-level package). The model rules in a project without models are unverifiable, which is why the scaffold keeps them commented out. See also ¶ Inspect an application : every hinoki check option. Authentication and access : what HNK-ACC-001/002 ask for. Build with a coding agent : the same diagnostics for agents through hinoki mcp .

docs.text: ID Rule Phase Checks HNK-ACC-001 Actions.require_access(match="*", except_=()) startup every matching action names an Access policy (public by default is the common hole) HNK-ACC-002 Actions.require_permissions(match="*", except_=()) startup an action with an Access policy names at least one permission, so "any authenticated caller" is never implicit HNK-API-001 Actions.forbid_model_responses(match="*", except_=()) startup no action returns a Model (or a list or page of them): responses are Schema classes HNK-API-002 Actions.require_return_type(match="*", except_=()) startup every action annotates a concrete return type (not missing, Any or object ; None is fine for a 204 ) HNK-API-003 Actions.require_pagination(match="*", except_=()) startup a GET action never returns a plain list[...] (alone or in a union): it returns a Page HNK-TXN-001 Transactions.require_atomic(methods=("POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"), match="*", except_=()) startup state-changing actions declare atomic=True , on the action or its RouteGroup HNK-SCH-001 Schemas.forbid_exposure(*fields) startup the named fields never appear in a response Schema : nested, in a subclass, in a union variant, as a field, an alias or a computed field HNK-SCH-002 Schemas.require_string_limits() startup every text field a client sends (nested, in containers, dict values and union variants included) has max_length or one_of ; Enum and Literal fields pass HNK-DB-001 Models.require_explicit_table(match="*") startup matching models pin their table with @db.table(...) or table= , so renaming the class cannot rename the table HNK-DB-002 Models.require_foreign_key_index(match="*") startup every foreign-key column leads an index, a primary key or a unique constraint HNK-IMP-001 Imports.forbid(source, target) static modules under source never import target , read from the source files; dynamic imports are reported, not ignored Every built-in rule has severity error . HNK-API-002 matters most for actions with validate_response=False : any other action with an unusable return annotation already stops the app. HNK-TXN-001 does not check the admin's own routes, which open their own short transactions.
docs.title: The eleven rules

docs.text: Action rules match fnmatch patterns against an action's qualified name: module.function for a function, module.Class.method for an API class (named after the class it is mounted on), and module.<Model>Crud.<action> for a crud(...) value, where module is the one that calls crud(...) . A bare health matches nothing; write notes.api.health or *.health . except_ takes the same patterns and is how you say "public on purpose". The Blog example names its exceptions once: # blog/rules.py PUBLIC = [ "blog.api.health" , "blog.api.Posts.listing" , "blog.api.Posts.one" , "blog.accounts.*.login" , # public on purpose: it is how you sign in ] SIGNED_IN = [ "blog.accounts.*.me" ] # any signed-in user, no permission blog_rules = RuleSet ( Actions . require_access ( match = "blog.*" , except_ = PUBLIC ), Actions . require_permissions ( match = "blog.*" , except_ = [ * PUBLIC , * SIGNED_IN ]), Transactions . require_atomic ( except_ = [ "blog.accounts.*.login" ]), Schemas . forbid_exposure ( "token" , "password_hash" ), Imports . forbid ( source = "blog.models" , target = "blog.api" ), # ... and the other six rules, see examples/blog/rules.py ) The model rules match the model's module ( blog.* ) and report unverifiable when no model matches, even with * . In a project with hinoki.toml , hinoki check first imports the models of every [[apps]] entry, so they are found without importing them from the application module. require_access and require_atomic report unverifiable when a pattern other than * matches no action. Neither passes silently.
docs.title: Choose what a rule covers

docs.text: Where Rules Waivers On failure Application startup ( hinoki dev , hinoki serve , any ASGI server, the test clients) startup rules of rules= the waiver file startup fails with RegistrationError listing every failing diagnostic hinoki check both phases (or --phase ) the waiver file, or --waivers exit code 1 hinoki mcp both phases the waiver file, or --waivers reported to the agent Startup enforcement means a broken promise never serves traffic. During a migration you can pass enforce_rules=False to Hinoki(...) : violations are then logged as a warning instead.
docs.title: When rules run

docs.text: hinoki check prints one line per finding, with its location and a fix: hint. This output comes from a deliberately broken project in Hinoki's own tests, checked from a clone of the repository: hinoki check tests.projects.rulesapp:create_app --rules tests.projects.rulesapp:rules tests/projects/rulesapp.py:7: HNK-ACC-001 [violated] GET /health (health) declares no access policy fix: add access=<policy> to the action (or list it in except_ when it is public on purpose) tests/projects/rulesapp.py:12: HNK-ACC-001 [violated] POST /items (create) declares no access policy fix: add access=<policy> to the action (or list it in except_ when it is public on purpose) tests/projects/rulesapp.py:12: HNK-TXN-001 [violated] POST /items (create) does not declare atomic=True fix: add atomic=True to the action (or declare it on a RouteGroup(..., atomic=True) group) 2 rule(s): 3 violated, 0 unverifiable, 0 waived Each status means one thing: violated (demonstrated), unverifiable (the check could not decide: a dynamic import, a pattern that matched nothing, a return type that does not name its schema, or a rule that crashed), waived and warning (a notice about the waiver file itself). Unverifiable fails like a violation; it is never a pass. A warning never fails. The fix line each rule prints: ID fix: HNK-ACC-002 name at least one permission in the Access policy of the action HNK-API-001 return a Schema (for example PostOut.from_model(row)) instead of the Model HNK-API-002 annotate the action's return type (a Schema, or None for status 204) HNK-API-003 return Page[Item] and paginate the action instead of returning a list HNK-SCH-001 remove the field from the response Schema, or return a Schema that does not carry it HNK-SCH-002 bound the field: Annotated[str, Field(max_length=...)] or one_of=... HNK-DB-001 name the table with @db.table(...) or table=... on the model HNK-DB-002 index the column: @db.indexed(" ") on the model, or an index or unique group that starts with it HNK-IMP-001 move the code to an allowed layer, or depend on it through the layer in between hinoki check --format json prints the same diagnostics as versioned data ( schema_version , rules , summary , and per diagnostic rule , severity , phase , status , message , location , explanation , subject , waiver , fix ) for CI, editors and agents. summary counts each status ( violated , unverifiable , waived , warning ) and adds failing , the number that sets the exit code. schema_version is 2 : version 1 reported waiver notices as violated and had no warning count. Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 failing, 2 the check could not run. The other options are on Inspect an application .
docs.title: Read the results

docs.text: Prefer except_ for things that are public or special by design . A waiver is for a known violation the owner accepts for a while. It lives in hinoki-rules.toml at the project root, which hinoki new creates: # hinoki-rules.toml [[waiver]] rule = "HNK-ACC-001" target = "tests.projects.rulesapp.health" reason = "liveness probe is public by design" owner = "platform-team" expires = 2027-01-31 rule , target , reason and owner are required. target is an fnmatch pattern on the diagnostic's subject and must be bounded: a literal prefix of at least five characters containing a dot ( shop.api.* , never * ). expires is optional and must be a TOML date, written without quotes; the waiver applies through that day and expires once the current UTC date is later. The waived diagnostic keeps its line and gains the decision: tests/projects/rulesapp.py:7: HNK-ACC-001 [waived] GET /health (health) declares no access policy fix: add access=<policy> to the action (or list it in except_ when it is public on purpose) waived: liveness probe is public by design (platform-team, until 2027-01-31) An expired waiver stops applying and reports HNK-WVR-002 ; one that matches nothing reports HNK-WVR-001 . Both have status warning : they print as [warning] , count under warning(s) in the summary ( summary.warning in JSON) and never change the exit code. A diagnostic that means "the rule could not do its job" cannot be waived. An invalid or unreadable file makes hinoki check exit with 2 .
docs.title: Accept an exception with a waiver

docs.text: hinoki check , hinoki mcp and application startup read the same file: The file named by Hinoki(waivers=...) , or by --waivers on check and mcp . A named file must exist. Otherwise hinoki-rules.toml at the project root: the directory of the nearest hinoki.toml , searched from the working directory upwards. Running from a subdirectory of the project finds the same file. Without a hinoki.toml , hinoki-rules.toml in the working directory. app = Hinoki ( rules = rules , waivers = "config/hinoki-rules.toml" ) A missing default file means no waivers. A directory or a broken symbolic link with that name is an error, not an absent file. hinoki mcp --waivers PATH also applies PATH to the app that run_scenario starts.
docs.title: Which waiver file

docs.text: Application startup applies the waiver file the same way as hinoki check . This app requires access on every action, yet it starts and serves /health because the owner waived it: # shop/main.py from hinoki import Actions , Hinoki , Request , http from hinoki.rules import RuleSet @http . get ( "/health" ) def health ( request : Request ) -> dict [ str , str ]: return { "status" : "ok" } app = Hinoki ( rules = RuleSet ( Actions . require_access ()), include = [ health ]) # hinoki-rules.toml [[waiver]] rule = "HNK-ACC-001" target = "shop.main.health" reason = "liveness probe is public by design" owner = "platform-team" Without the waiver, hinoki serve fails at startup with RegistrationError: 1 rule violation(s) . At startup: An absent default file means no waivers. An invalid or unreadable file, or a missing file named with waivers= , fails startup with RegistrationError ("invalid waivers: .../hinoki-rules.toml: waiver #1: missing target"), even with enforce_rules=False . An expired waiver does not apply: the violation fails startup and the RegistrationError also lists the HNK-WVR-002 notice. Without a remaining violation the notice is logged as a warning. HNK-WVR-001 (unused waiver) is reported only by hinoki check and hinoki mcp : startup runs only the startup rules, so a waiver for a static rule such as HNK-IMP-001 is expected to match nothing there. Waivers are the owner's decision: tools read the file and never write it. Put it under CODEOWNERS; the generated AGENTS.md tells agents the same.
docs.title: Waivers at startup

docs.text: Subclass hinoki.rules.Rule with a stable id , an explanation , an optional fix and a check that yields diagnostics. phase defaults to Phase.STARTUP and severity to Severity.ERROR . # notes/rules.py from collections.abc import Iterator from hinoki.rules import Diagnostic , Project , Rule , qualified , where class NoDelete ( Rule ): id = "NOTES-API-001" explanation = "This project archives rows instead of deleting them." fix = "use PATCH to set archived=true" def check ( self , project : Project ) -> Iterator [ Diagnostic ]: for route in project . app . routes : if route . method == "DELETE" : yield self . diagnostic ( f "DELETE { route . path } removes a row" , where ( route . handler ), subject = qualified ( route ), ) Add NoDelete() to the RuleSet . where(obj) gives a file:line location; qualified(route) gives the subject that waivers match (without a subject the location is used; an empty subject cannot be waived). A rule that needs side effects (running code, files, network, a database) lists them in effects and only runs under hinoki check --allow-effects ; at startup it is refused and reported as unverifiable. RuleSet raises ValueError for an empty ID or the same ID twice.
docs.title: Your own rules

docs.text: A rule that raises is reported as unverifiable with "the rule failed to run", never skipped. HNK-IMP-001 runs only in hinoki check and hinoki mcp ; it needs the source files of the checked packages ( --package , default: the target's top-level package). The model rules in a project without models are unverifiable, which is why the scaffold keeps them commented out.

docs.text: Native CRUD phase 1: end-to-end orientation run ¶ This is one host-specific orientation measurement, not a performance claim or a framework ranking. The primary table reports five alternating pairs of Hinoki's automatically selected Rust generated CRUD path (declared with the since-removed CrudAPI class when measured; crud(...) now generates the same routes) and a manually implemented equivalent Django Bolt endpoint. Both apps use the same PostgreSQL table and deterministic 10,000-row seed. Their list, detail, create and update responses were verified against the database before timing. Run started: 2026-11-18T03:09:11.864738+00:00. Host: Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10300H CPU @ 2.50GHz (8 logical CPUs), Linux-7.2.11-arch1-1-x86_64-with-glibc2.44; Python 3.13.18; PostgreSQL postgres (PostgreSQL) 17.12 (Debian 17.12-1.pgdg13+1); Rust rustc 1.100.0 (0ef1bc386 2026-11-09); Oha oha 1.17.0. Hinoki 0.0.1 uses Kiso and tokio-postgres; Django Bolt 0.13.0 uses Django 6.1.3 with psycopg 3.3.9 and its Actix server. Each starts 4 processes with a pool of 10 database connections per process. Scenarios: list page sizes 20 and 100, detail, create and PATCH update. Each sample has 10 s warm-up, then 20 s measured with 64 concurrent connections. Server CPUs: 0-3; load generator CPUs: 6-7; response compression disabled. Each sample's one-minute host load is checked before its server starts and must be at most 1.0. Across the samples, scenario start loads ranged from 0.81 to 1.00. SQL calls are read from pg_stat_statements after each timed request window; the table reports the median calls per successful HTTP request. The samples are not a universal ranking and do not establish production performance. Host, OS, Python, server, ORM, driver, database, warm-cache state, and workload all affect these results. CV above 15% marks that scenario as unstable for interpretation; no sample is dropped. Raw oha JSON, per-sample start-load metadata and SQL stats, server logs, environment metadata, verifier output, request bodies, and the machine-readable summary are retained in benchmarks/comparative/results/2026-11-18/crud-phase1/ . Reproduction: build the native extension in release mode, start an isolated PostgreSQL 17 container, then run phase1_orientation.py as documented in benchmarks/README.md . The script refuses to time a sample whose starting load is above 1.0. Supplemental samples ¶ Because the initial list_100 Hinoki CV exceeded 15%, five additional alternating pairs (6-10) were collected separately. This block is not pooled into the primary table: Scenario Hinoki median req/s (range, CV) Django Bolt median req/s (range, CV) list_100, pairs 6-10 5088.4 (5073.4-5128.2, 0.4%) 2080.8 (2066.3-2085.8, 0.4%) The supplemental block is internally stable, while the initial Hinoki list_100 series remains unstable and shows a change in throughput regime. Treat both blocks as host-specific orientation data; the stable follow-up does not erase the initial variance. The supplemental update series stopped at Hinoki pair 7 after unsuccessful responses (status distribution: 200 = 3,554, 500 = 20). Its server log reports database connection acquisition timeouts. The failed sample and log are retained and excluded from throughput summaries; the initial update series remains volatile (Hinoki CV 11.8%, Django Bolt CV 23.5%).

docs.text: Collections and unions ¶ A field can hold list[X] , set[X] , frozenset[X] , tuple[X, ...] , tuple[X, Y] , dict[str, X] , a nested Schema , a TypedDict , a dataclass, a plain union, a discriminated union or Any . X is any supported type, so list[dict[str, int]] works. Error paths add [index] for items and .key for entries: rows[1][0].x , points.gate.x . Sets and tuples ¶ from typing import Annotated from hinoki import Field , Schema class Place ( Schema ): tags : Annotated [ set [ str ], Field ( max_length = 5 )] point : tuple [ float , float ] path : tuple [ int , ... ] = () place = Place . validate ({ "tags" : [ "a" , "b" , "a" ], "point" : [ 1.5 , 2 ]}) assert place . tags == { "a" , "b" } and place . point == ( 1.5 , 2.0 ) assert place . dump () == { "tags" : [ "a" , "b" ], "point" : [ 1.5 , 2.0 ], "path" : []} They travel as JSON arrays. Set duplicates collapse; length limits count the array as sent. A fixed tuple's length comes from its type and refuses Field(...) . Set items must be hashable (scalars, enums, tuples and frozensets of those). Bare set , tuple[()] and a misplaced ... raise RegistrationError . Construction takes exactly the declared container; to_dict() keeps it, dump() writes arrays (sets sorted when comparable). No model column type: store a list[X] (JSON) and build sets in the Schema . Served by the Python lane. OpenAPI: uniqueItems for sets; prefixItems , minItems , maxItems for fixed tuples. Dictionary fields ¶ from typing import Annotated from hinoki import Field , Schema Locale = Annotated [ str , Field ( min_length = 2 , max_length = 5 , pattern = r "[a-z] {2} (-[A-Z] {2} )?" ) ] Label = Annotated [ str , Field ( max_length = 40 )] Name = Annotated [ str , Field ( max_length = 80 )] class Point ( Schema ): x : int y : int = 0 class Venue ( Schema ): labels : Annotated [ dict [ str , Label ], Field ( max_length = 20 )] names : dict [ Locale , Name ] = Field ( default_factory = dict ) points : dict [ str , Point ] = Field ( default_factory = dict ) venue = Venue . validate ({ "labels" : { "kind" : "park" }, "points" : { "gate" : { "x" : 1 }}}) assert venue . points == { "gate" : Point ( x = 1 )} Keys are strings. dict[int, X] , dict[UUID, X] and bare dict are refused at class creation. Constrain keys with dict[Annotated[str, Field(...)], X] ( min_length , max_length , pattern , format ); a bad key answers key_min_length , key_max_length or key_pattern and its value is not checked. Entry count. Field(min_length=, max_length=) on the dict counts entries. Client input is bounded. Without max_length , wire input accepts at most 1000 entries ( MAX_MAPPING_ITEMS ) and keys of at most 256 characters ( MAX_MAPPING_KEY_LENGTH ); declared limits replace these. Values the server builds (construction, from_model() ) are not bounded. Order is kept as sent; a repeated JSON key keeps its first position and last value. Paths shorten keys longer than 64 characters. Models. A dict column is a JSON column: model writes do not apply these checks. A Schema derived from it validates as above without wire bounds. HNK-SCH-002 checks text values for limits; HNK-SCH-001 checks field names only, not keys. OpenAPI: type: object with additionalProperties , propertyNames and declared minProperties / maxProperties . Plain unions and Any ¶ from typing import Annotated , Any from hinoki import Field , Schema class Reading ( Schema ): value : int | str when : Annotated [ int , Field ( ge = 0 )] | Annotated [ str , Field ( max_length = 10 )] extra : Any = None reading = Reading . validate ({ "value" : "abc" , "when" : 5 , "extra" : { "k" : [ 1 , None ]}}) assert reading . value == "abc" and reading . when == 5 First match wins , in declared order; bool is never an int . No match answers union once at the field path. 2 to 16 variants; constraints go on a variant, not the union. A union of only Schema classes needs a discriminator (below). Any and object accept every JSON value unchanged; bound their size elsewhere. Text sources take the first int , float or bool variant that parses, else the str variant. More than 1024 failed container trials inside one union refuse the request. Checked in Rust on the Python-object path; not lowered to the GIL-free JSON lane. OpenAPI: anyOf . Model columns with a union or Any are refused by migrations. Discriminated unions ¶ from typing import Annotated from hinoki import Field , Schema class Card ( Schema ): kind : Annotated [ str , Field ( alias = "type" , one_of = ( "card" ,))] last4 : Annotated [ str , Field ( min_length = 4 , max_length = 4 )] class Transfer ( Schema ): kind : Annotated [ str , Field ( alias = "type" , one_of = ( "transfer" ,))] iban : Annotated [ str , Field ( max_length = 34 )] Method = Annotated [ Card | Transfer , Field ( discriminator = "kind" )] class PaymentIn ( Schema ): method : Method PaymentIn.validate({"method": {"type": "card", "last4": "4242"}}) returns a Card , selected by its tag in Rust without trying each variant. Every variant has the same required string tag field (no default), the same alias, and exactly one Field(one_of=(...)) value; tags are unique and variants distinct. An unknown tag is a field error at the tag's wire path, without echoing the value. Construction takes a variant instance, never a dict. Variants cannot override dump() . list[Method] , nested fields, | None and | Unset follow the same rules. A union directly in a handler's body or return annotation is not supported: wrap it in a Schema . TypedDict and dataclass fields ¶ from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import NotRequired , TypedDict from hinoki import Schema class Address ( TypedDict ): street : str zip : NotRequired [ str ] @dataclass class Geo : lat : float lon : float = 0.0 class Site ( Schema ): address : Address geo : Geo | None = None Hinoki generates one Schema per type with the same name and fields; the value is an instance of it ( site.address.street ), not a dict or Geo . Methods, __post_init__ and bases are not carried over. A key that may be missing becomes | Unset ; a dataclass field with a default is optional. Member Field(...) constraints are honoured. init=False and recursive types raise RegistrationError . OpenAPI: one component named after the type. See also ¶ Scalar field types Validate input OpenAPI

docs.text: from typing import Annotated from hinoki import Field , Schema Locale = Annotated [ str , Field ( min_length = 2 , max_length = 5 , pattern = r "[a-z] {2} (-[A-Z] {2} )?" ) ] Label = Annotated [ str , Field ( max_length = 40 )] Name = Annotated [ str , Field ( max_length = 80 )] class Point ( Schema ): x : int y : int = 0 class Venue ( Schema ): labels : Annotated [ dict [ str , Label ], Field ( max_length = 20 )] names : dict [ Locale , Name ] = Field ( default_factory = dict ) points : dict [ str , Point ] = Field ( default_factory = dict ) venue = Venue . validate ({ "labels" : { "kind" : "park" }, "points" : { "gate" : { "x" : 1 }}}) assert venue . points == { "gate" : Point ( x = 1 )} Keys are strings. dict[int, X] , dict[UUID, X] and bare dict are refused at class creation. Constrain keys with dict[Annotated[str, Field(...)], X] ( min_length , max_length , pattern , format ); a bad key answers key_min_length , key_max_length or key_pattern and its value is not checked. Entry count. Field(min_length=, max_length=) on the dict counts entries. Client input is bounded. Without max_length , wire input accepts at most 1000 entries ( MAX_MAPPING_ITEMS ) and keys of at most 256 characters ( MAX_MAPPING_KEY_LENGTH ); declared limits replace these. Values the server builds (construction, from_model() ) are not bounded. Order is kept as sent; a repeated JSON key keeps its first position and last value. Paths shorten keys longer than 64 characters. Models. A dict column is a JSON column: model writes do not apply these checks. A Schema derived from it validates as above without wire bounds. HNK-SCH-002 checks text values for limits; HNK-SCH-001 checks field names only, not keys. OpenAPI: type: object with additionalProperties , propertyNames and declared minProperties / maxProperties .

docs.text: from typing import Annotated , Any from hinoki import Field , Schema class Reading ( Schema ): value : int | str when : Annotated [ int , Field ( ge = 0 )] | Annotated [ str , Field ( max_length = 10 )] extra : Any = None reading = Reading . validate ({ "value" : "abc" , "when" : 5 , "extra" : { "k" : [ 1 , None ]}}) assert reading . value == "abc" and reading . when == 5 First match wins , in declared order; bool is never an int . No match answers union once at the field path. 2 to 16 variants; constraints go on a variant, not the union. A union of only Schema classes needs a discriminator (below). Any and object accept every JSON value unchanged; bound their size elsewhere. Text sources take the first int , float or bool variant that parses, else the str variant. More than 1024 failed container trials inside one union refuse the request. Checked in Rust on the Python-object path; not lowered to the GIL-free JSON lane. OpenAPI: anyOf . Model columns with a union or Any are refused by migrations.
docs.title: Plain unions and Any

docs.text: from typing import Annotated from hinoki import Field , Schema class Card ( Schema ): kind : Annotated [ str , Field ( alias = "type" , one_of = ( "card" ,))] last4 : Annotated [ str , Field ( min_length = 4 , max_length = 4 )] class Transfer ( Schema ): kind : Annotated [ str , Field ( alias = "type" , one_of = ( "transfer" ,))] iban : Annotated [ str , Field ( max_length = 34 )] Method = Annotated [ Card | Transfer , Field ( discriminator = "kind" )] class PaymentIn ( Schema ): method : Method PaymentIn.validate({"method": {"type": "card", "last4": "4242"}}) returns a Card , selected by its tag in Rust without trying each variant. Every variant has the same required string tag field (no default), the same alias, and exactly one Field(one_of=(...)) value; tags are unique and variants distinct. An unknown tag is a field error at the tag's wire path, without echoing the value. Construction takes a variant instance, never a dict. Variants cannot override dump() . list[Method] , nested fields, | None and | Unset follow the same rules. A union directly in a handler's body or return annotation is not supported: wrap it in a Schema .
docs.title: Discriminated unions

docs.text: from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import NotRequired , TypedDict from hinoki import Schema class Address ( TypedDict ): street : str zip : NotRequired [ str ] @dataclass class Geo : lat : float lon : float = 0.0 class Site ( Schema ): address : Address geo : Geo | None = None Hinoki generates one Schema per type with the same name and fields; the value is an instance of it ( site.address.street ), not a dict or Geo . Methods, __post_init__ and bases are not carried over. A key that may be missing becomes | Unset ; a dataclass field with a default is optional. Member Field(...) constraints are honoured. init=False and recursive types raise RegistrationError . OpenAPI: one component named after the type.
