docs.text: Models and queries ¶ Concrete models may omit @db.table(...) (or the compatible table= class keyword) to derive the table name <app>_<models> from the model's package and class name; label= and plural= override humanized display names. Explicit table names remain the safe choice for migration-backed histories and stable physical names. hinoki.orm.Model ¶ Base class: class Post(Model): ... with an optional table= override. NotFound class-attribute ¶ NotFound : type [ ObjectNotFound ] = ObjectNotFound is_new property ¶ is_new : bool True until the row has been written or loaded. is_dirty property ¶ is_dirty : bool True for a new instance and for one whose columns differ from the stored values. changes property ¶ changes : dict [ str , Change ] The columns that differ from the stored row, as Change(old, new) . A new instance reports every column with old=UNSET . Computed when read: nothing is tracked on assignment. check_field_conflicts classmethod ¶ check_field_conflicts () -> None Two bases may not give one field name different types: which one the model would get depends on base order, and the other would be lost. A base that overrides its own parent, or the class redeclaring the field, is a decision and is accepted. check_field_validations classmethod ¶ check_field_validations ( columns : tuple [ Field [ Any ], ... ], annotations : dict [ str , object ], ) -> dict [ str , FieldType ] Validate constraints against annotations and reject async callbacks. validate_values classmethod ¶ validate_values ( values : dict [ str , Any ]) -> None Run declared field checks on values about to be written. adopt_mixin_fields classmethod ¶ adopt_mixin_fields () -> None Field annotations of plain (non-model, non-dataclass) bases become fields of this class. dataclasses reads only a class's own annotations and its dataclass bases, so without this a mixin's fields would be dropped without a word. option_bases classmethod ¶ option_bases () -> list [ type [ Model ]] The abstract models this class is declared on. Each already holds what it inherited and what it replaced, so nothing further up is read again; a concrete parent keeps its options to itself. inherit_options classmethod ¶ inherit_options ( unique : Sequence [ Sequence [ str ]]) -> None Options come from the abstract bases the class lists: every such base's constraints and indexes, and the first one that sets an order or a timestamp column. A decorator applied to this class later replaces what was inherited for its kind (see hinoki.orm.options ). Indexes declared with field(index=True) belong to their column: they stay while the column keeps index=True and go when this class redeclares the column without it, whether or not a decorator is applied. keeps_index classmethod ¶ keeps_index ( base : type [ Model ], columns : tuple [ str , ... ] ) -> bool Whether an index of base carries over: a decorator index always does, a field(index=True) index only while this class's column still declares it. check_table classmethod ¶ check_table () -> None Raise the deferred error of a derived table name that cannot be used: the class name gave no portable or free name and no @db.table / table= replaced it. replace_inherited classmethod ¶ replace_inherited ( kind : str ) -> bool True the first time an option of kind is applied to a class that inherited that kind: the caller then starts from nothing. concrete classmethod ¶ concrete () -> type [ Self ] This class, refusing an abstract model: it has no table to query. check_unique classmethod ¶ check_unique ( groups : Sequence [ Sequence [ str ]], ) -> tuple [ tuple [ str , ... ], ... ] Composite uniqueness, e.g. unique=[("post_id", "tag_id")] on a many-to-many join model. Single columns use field(unique=True) . check_names classmethod ¶ check_names ( columns : tuple [ str , ... ]) -> None A column named like a Model method would hide it on every instance. check_set_null classmethod ¶ check_set_null ( column : Field [ Any ], meta : FieldMeta ) -> None set_null on a column that cannot hold NULL fails every delete of the referenced row, so it is refused when the model is declared. An annotation that cannot be resolved yet is left to the migration plan. register_relations classmethod ¶ register_relations ( fields : tuple [ Field [ Any ], ... ]) -> None Foreign keys this class declares or takes from an abstract base or a mixin (those of a concrete parent come with it). Every check runs before anything is attached, so a failing definition leaves the referenced models untouched. reverse_name classmethod ¶ reverse_name ( column : str , related_name : str ) -> str related_name with {model} replaced by this class's name in lower case, so one declaration in an abstract base or a mixin gives each concrete model its own reverse relation. check_attach classmethod ¶ check_attach ( name : str , relation : Relation ) -> None attach classmethod ¶ attach ( name : str , relation : Relation ) -> None row_plan classmethod ¶ row_plan () -> core . _ModelRows | None The native row builder for this model, or None when its instances must go through from_row (a custom constructor or allocator, columns that need a reader, or an overridden or patched from_row , remember or __post_init__ ). The builder is made once per class; the cheap override checks run on every call. from_row classmethod ¶ from_row ( row : dict [ str , Any ]) -> Self remember ¶ remember () -> None Record the stored values, so asave writes only what changed. was_changed ¶ was_changed ( name : str ) -> bool Whether column name differs from the stored row (always True for a new instance). after_commit ¶ after_commit ( callback : Callable [[], object ]) -> None Run callback (sync or async) once the surrounding transaction commits; never after a rollback. Meant for after_* hooks. before_save ¶ before_save () -> Awaitable [ None ] | None Hook: runs before every write of this instance; values may still change. before_create ¶ before_create () -> Awaitable [ None ] | None Hook: runs before a new instance is first written, after before_save . after_create ¶ after_create () -> Awaitable [ None ] | None Hook: runs after the row is inserted, before after_save . after_save ¶ after_save () -> Awaitable [ None ] | None Hook: runs after the row is written, inside the transaction. write_hooks classmethod ¶ write_hooks () -> tuple [ str , ... ] The hooks this model overrides, looked up on each write so a hook assigned after the class was created is not missed. hook_transaction staticmethod ¶ hook_transaction () -> AbstractAsyncContextManager [ Any ] The transaction a hooked write runs in: a savepoint when one is open (see write_transaction ). run_hooks async ¶ run_hooks ( * names : str ) -> None Run the overridden hooks among names , def or async def . asave async ¶ asave () -> Self Insert a new instance, or update the columns changed since it was loaded. Typed: Post(title="x", ...) is checked by the type checker. save_with async ¶ save_with ( scope : QuerySet [ Any ] | None ) -> Self asave ; with scope the UPDATE carries that query's conditions, so a row that left the scope since it was read is refused ( Model.NotFound ) instead of written. aupdate_within async ¶ aupdate_within ( scope : QuerySet [ Any ], / , ** values : Any ) -> Self assign then a save whose UPDATE carries scope 's conditions (the generated CRUD update uses it so ownership and visibility hold at write time). A failed write leaves the instance as it was. write_update async ¶ write_update ( scope : QuerySet [ Any ] | None = None ) -> bool Write the changed columns and load the stored row, without taking a new snapshot; False when nothing changed. insert async ¶ insert ( * , returning : bool = True ) -> Self Insert this instance and load the stored row into it. With returning=False nothing is read back: the instance keeps the values it sent (every column is sent, defaults and factories applied). write_insert async ¶ write_insert ( returning : bool ) -> None load_stored ¶ load_stored ( stored : Model ) -> None save ¶ save () -> Self related ¶ related ( name : str ) -> Any The loaded relation name ( RelationNotLoaded if it was not). filter classmethod ¶ filter ( ** conditions : Any ) -> QuerySet [ Self ] all classmethod ¶ all () -> QuerySet [ Self ] from_schema classmethod ¶ from_schema ( data : Schema | None = None , / , ** values : Any ) -> Self An unsaved instance from a schema's values plus values . Explicit keyword values win over the schema's, so a column the server assigns (owner, state) can never come from the client. acreate async classmethod ¶ acreate ( data : Schema | None = None , / , * , returning : bool = True , ** values : Any , ) -> Self Insert a row (defaults and factories apply) and return it: await Post.acreate(data, author_id=me) or acreate(title="x") . returning=False : the instance holds the sent values, not re-read. assign ¶ assign ( data : Schema | None = None , / , ** values : Any ) -> Self Set fields from a schema (fields the client left UNSET are untouched) and keyword values, without touching the database. aupdate_from async ¶ aupdate_from ( data : Schema | None = None , / , ** values : Any ) -> Self assign then asave : only the columns that changed are written. aget async classmethod ¶ aget ( ** conditions : Any ) -> Self Exactly one row, else Model.NotFound / MultipleObjectsReturned . aget_or_none async classmethod ¶ aget_or_none ( ** conditions : Any ) -> Self | None aupdate async classmethod ¶ aupdate ( * , returning : Literal [ True ] = ... , ** values : Any ) -> Self aupdate ( * , returning : Literal [ False ], ** values : Any ) -> int aupdate ( * , returning : bool , ** values : Any ) -> Self | int aupdate ( * , returning : bool = True , ** values : Any ) -> Self | int Update by primary key ( id=... ) and return the updated row. returning=False reads nothing back and returns the row count the database reports (no NotFound : 0 means no row was written). aupdate_where async classmethod ¶ aupdate_where ( conditions : dict [ str , Any ], values : dict [ str , Any ], * , returning : Literal [ True ] = ... , ) -> list [ Self ] aupdate_where ( conditions : dict [ str , Any ], values : dict [ str , Any ], * , returning : Literal [ False ], ) -> int aupdate_where ( conditions : dict [ str , Any ], values : dict [ str , Any ], * , returning : bool , ) -> list [ Self ] | int aupdate_where ( conditions : dict [ str , Any ], values : dict [ str , Any ], * , returning : bool = True , ) -> list [ Self ] | int Update every row matching conditions and return the new rows (or, with returning=False , the row count the database reports). Conditions are part of the statement, so a row that stopped matching (for example after a concurrent owner change) is not touched. adelete async classmethod ¶ adelete ( ** conditions : Any ) -> int Delete matching rows; returns how many. An empty condition set is refused so a missing filter cannot wipe the table. abulk_create async classmethod ¶ abulk_create ( items : Iterable [ Schema | dict [ str , Any ]], / , * , returning : bool = True , ) -> list [ Self ] Insert many rows in one transaction: all of them or none. Each item is a Schema or a dict of field values; defaults, factories, validation and write hooks apply exactly as for acreate . Returns the rows in order. bulk_instances classmethod ¶ bulk_instances ( items : Iterable [ Schema | dict [ str , Any ]], ) -> list [ Self ] The unsaved instances abulk_create inserts, checked before writing. insert_all async staticmethod ¶ insert_all ( instances : list [ M ], * , returning : bool ) -> list [ M ] Insert instances in the caller's transaction. abulk_update async classmethod ¶ abulk_update ( instances : Iterable [ Self ]) -> list [ Self ] Save the changes of many loaded instances in one transaction: all of them or none. Unchanged instances write nothing; an unsaved one is refused. saved_rows classmethod ¶ saved_rows ( instances : Iterable [ Self ]) -> list [ Self ] The instances abulk_update saves; an unsaved one is refused. save_all async staticmethod ¶ save_all ( rows : list [ M ]) -> list [ M ] Save rows in the caller's transaction. abulk_delete async classmethod ¶ abulk_delete ( items : Iterable [ Self | Any ]) -> int Delete many rows by instance or primary-key value in one transaction; returns how many existed. Nothing is deleted for an empty list. delete_key classmethod ¶ delete_key ( item : Self | Any ) -> Any The primary-key value abulk_delete removes for item . create classmethod ¶ create ( data : Schema | None = None , / , * , returning : bool = True , ** values : Any , ) -> Self Sync acreate for sync handlers. update_from ¶ update_from ( data : Schema | None = None , / , ** values : Any ) -> Self Sync aupdate_from for sync handlers. update_where classmethod ¶ update_where ( conditions : dict [ str , Any ], values : dict [ str , Any ], * , returning : Literal [ True ] = ... , ) -> list [ Self ] update_where ( conditions : dict [ str , Any ], values : dict [ str , Any ], * , returning : Literal [ False ], ) -> int update_where ( conditions : dict [ str , Any ], values : dict [ str , Any ], * , returning : bool , ) -> list [ Self ] | int update_where ( conditions : dict [ str , Any ], values : dict [ str , Any ], * , returning : bool = True , ) -> list [ Self ] | int Sync aupdate_where for sync handlers. get classmethod ¶ get ( ** conditions : Any ) -> Self get_or_none classmethod ¶ get_or_none ( ** conditions : Any ) -> Self | None update classmethod ¶ update ( * , returning : Literal [ True ] = ... , ** values : Any ) -> Self update ( * , returning : Literal [ False ], ** values : Any ) -> int update ( * , returning : bool , ** values : Any ) -> Self | int update ( * , returning : bool = True , ** values : Any ) -> Self | int Sync aupdate for sync handlers. delete classmethod ¶ delete ( ** conditions : Any ) -> int bulk_create classmethod ¶ bulk_create ( items : Iterable [ Schema | dict [ str , Any ]], / , * , returning : bool = True , ) -> list [ Self ] Sync abulk_create for sync handlers; inside an open transaction it is a savepoint of that transaction (see run_bulk ). bulk_update classmethod ¶ bulk_update ( instances : Iterable [ Self ]) -> list [ Self ] Sync abulk_update for sync handlers; scoped as bulk_create . bulk_delete classmethod ¶ bulk_delete ( items : Iterable [ Self | Any ]) -> int Sync abulk_delete for sync handlers; scoped as bulk_create . merged_values classmethod ¶ merged_values ( data : Schema | None , values : dict [ str , Any ] ) -> dict [ str , Any ] The schema's values with explicit values winning, every name checked. A schema may never carry the primary key: the client must not choose a row's identity (pass it as a keyword when the server does). check_field classmethod ¶ check_field ( name : str ) -> None hinoki.orm.field ¶ field ( * , primary_key : bool = False , unique : bool = False , index : bool = False , max_length : int | None = None , constraints : FieldInfo | None = None , validators : Sequence [ Callable [ ... , None ]] = (), default : Any = dataclasses . MISSING , default_factory : Callable [[], Any ] | Any = dataclasses . MISSING , ) -> Any Declare a column and, optionally, write-time constraints and validators. id: UUID = field(primary_key=True, default_factory=uuid4) name: str = field(constraints=Field(min_length=1), validators=(check_name,)) created_at: datetime = field(index=True, default_factory=utc_now) adds a single-column index, the same index as @db.indexed("created_at") . Constraints run before ORM writes. Custom validators are synchronous and raise ValueError to refuse a value; they must not perform I/O. hinoki.orm.pk ¶ pk ( * , max_length : int | None = None , constraints : FieldInfo | None = None , validators : Sequence [ Callable [ ... , None ]] = (), default : Any = dataclasses . MISSING , default_factory : Callable [[], Any ] | Any = dataclasses . MISSING , ) -> Any Declare the primary key: shorthand for field(primary_key=True, ...) . id: UUID = pk(default_factory=uuid4) It takes the options of field that make sense for a key; unique and index are implied by the primary key. Model write validation raises ModelValidationError from hinoki.errors , with field paths, stable codes and messages in details . See Model field constraints and validators . hinoki.orm.foreign_key ¶ foreign_key ( model : type [ Model ], * , on_delete : OnDelete , related_name : str = "" , unique : bool = False , validators : Sequence [ Callable [ ... , None ]] = (), default : Any = dataclasses . MISSING , ) -> Any Declare a column that references model 's primary key. author_id: UUID = foreign_key(User, on_delete=OnDelete.RESTRICT) on_delete is required and is an OnDelete member ( RESTRICT , CASCADE , SET_NULL or NO_ACTION ), so a deletion rule is always a decision; text such as "cascade" is refused. SET_NULL needs a column annotated | None . The relation is named after the column without _id and is loaded only by select_related / prefetch_related . hinoki.orm.OnDelete ¶ Bases: Enum What the database does with the rows that reference a deleted row. RESTRICT class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ RESTRICT = 'restrict' Refuse the delete while referencing rows exist. CASCADE class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ CASCADE = 'cascade' Delete the referencing rows too. SET_NULL class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ SET_NULL = 'set_null' Set the column to NULL; the field must be annotated | None . NO_ACTION class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ NO_ACTION = 'no_action' Like RESTRICT , checked by the database at the end of the statement. hinoki.orm.unique ¶ unique ( * columns : str , name : str | None = None ) -> Callable [[ M ], M ] A composite uniqueness constraint over two or more columns (single columns use field(unique=True) ). name names the constraint in the database; without it the backend chooses one. hinoki.orm.indexed ¶ indexed ( * columns : str ) -> Callable [[ M ], M ] A (non-unique) index over one or more columns, created by the migration planner. A single column can use field(index=True) instead; naming a column both ways creates one index. hinoki.orm.table ¶ table ( name : str ) -> Callable [[ M ], M ] Name the model's table; without it the name is derived from the class name. @table("saved_links") is the same as table="saved_links" in the class header; giving both with different names is an error. hinoki.orm.ordered_by ¶ ordered_by ( * names : str ) -> Callable [[ M ], M ] The default order of every query that does not call order_by ; "-created_at" is descending. hinoki.orm.timestamps ¶ timestamps ( updated_at : str = "updated_at" , * , clock : Clock = utc_now , ) -> Callable [[ M ], M ] Update a declared datetime column on each ORM update statement. Timestamp columns remain ordinary model fields, visible to type checkers and migrations. Declare their creation defaults with utc_now . A count needs only the filtered ones: loading a to-one relation cannot change the number of rows. compile ¶ compile ( kind : str = "select" , dialect : str = "postgres" ) -> tuple [ str , list [ Any ]] build ¶ build ( row : dict [ str , Any ]) -> M load async ¶ load ( instances : list [ M ]) -> None prefetch async ¶ prefetch ( name : str , instances : list [ M ]) -> None prefetch_forward async ¶ prefetch_forward ( relation : Relation , instances : list [ M ] ) -> None prefetch_reverse async ¶ prefetch_reverse ( relation : Relation , instances : list [ M ] ) -> None uses_stock_builders ¶ uses_stock_builders () -> bool False when build or _hydrate was overridden or patched: the native row builder would silently skip that code. fetch async ¶ fetch () -> list [ M ] Run the query and build the rows; what await queryset returns. afirst async ¶ afirst () -> M | None aget async ¶ aget () -> M aupdate async ¶ aupdate ( values : dict [ str , Any ], * , returning : Literal [ True ] = ... , ) -> builtins . list [ M ] aupdate ( values : dict [ str , Any ], * , returning : Literal [ False ] ) -> int aupdate ( values : dict [ str , Any ], * , returning : bool ) -> builtins . list [ M ] | int aupdate ( values : dict [ str , Any ], * , returning : bool = True ) -> builtins . list [ M ] | int Update the rows this query matches (its filters are part of the statement) and return them. docs.text: Schemas ¶ hinoki.schema.Schema ¶ Base class for schemas. class PostCreate(Schema): title: str becomes a frozen, keyword-only dataclass. PostCreate.validate(data) checks decoded JSON strictly: no coercion, unknown keys refused by default, and every problem reported with its path. is_generic classmethod ¶ is_generic () -> bool True while type parameters are still open ( Envelope ). computed_fields classmethod ¶ computed_fields () -> dict [ str , ComputedSpec ] The read-only values this schema adds to its output, by name. apply_default classmethod ¶ apply_default ( name : str ) -> None Turn a Field(default_factory=...) attribute into a dataclass default. specs classmethod ¶ specs () -> dict [ str , FieldSpec ] Field descriptions, resolving forward references on first use. build_specs classmethod ¶ build_specs ( final : bool = False ) -> dict [ str , FieldSpec ] validate_normalizers classmethod ¶ validate_normalizers ( specs : dict [ str , FieldSpec ]) -> None Check that registered normalizers have a precise typed target. native_schema classmethod ¶ native_schema () -> core . CompiledSchema The Rust validator for this schema and everything it refers to, compiled on first use and cached on the class. validate classmethod ¶ validate ( data : object ) -> Self Build an instance from decoded JSON or raise ValidationError (validated in Rust). validate_text classmethod ¶ validate_text ( data : object ) -> Self Like validate for data that is all text, such as form fields ( {"count": ["2"]} ) or a parsed XML tree: text is first converted, in Rust, to the int , float and bool the fields declare. Anything that does not convert is left for validate to refuse. Before hooks see the raw text (each form value is a list of strings) and run first. fields classmethod ¶ fields () -> dict [ str , FieldSpec ] Immutable description shared by binding, docs and rules. to_dict ¶ to_dict ( * , exclude : Iterable [ str ] = ()) -> dict [ str , Any ] The field values as Python objects (UUID, datetime stay what they are), nested schemas converted too. Fields left UNSET are omitted, so the result is exactly "what the client sent" for a partial update. replace ¶ replace ( ** changes : Any ) -> Self A copy with changes (Python field names) applied. Every value is validated again, normalised and checked like a new instance, so the copy is as trustworthy as any other; fields that were never supplied stay unsupplied for dump(exclude_unset=True) . from_models classmethod ¶ from_models ( rows : Iterable [ object ], ** extra : Any ) -> list [ Self ] Build a list from a synchronous iterable of model rows. Each row follows from_model exactly. The iterable is consumed once, eagerly; this reads already-loaded attributes and never performs I/O. from_model classmethod ¶ from_model ( row : object , ** extra : Any ) -> Self Build this schema from a model instance: every field is read from the attribute of the same name, extra supplies or overrides values (for computed fields). Nested models become nested schemas. A field the row lacks is an error, and an unloaded relation still raises RelationNotLoaded : nothing here does I/O. dump ¶ dump ( * , include : Iterable [ str ] | None = None , exclude : Iterable [ str ] = (), exclude_unset : bool = False , by_alias : bool = True , ) -> dict [ str , Any ] Return JSON-compatible data with optional projection controls. Selectors use Python field names. exclude_unset omits defaulted fields not supplied at construction. HTTP responses use default options. hinoki.schemaconfig.SchemaConfig dataclass ¶ SchemaConfig ( * , extra : SchemaExtra = SchemaExtra . FORBID ) Immutable class-level Schema behavior configuration. hinoki.schemaconfig.SchemaExtra ¶ Bases: StrEnum Policy for unknown string keys in decoded Schema input. hinoki.fields.Field ¶ Field ( * , default_factory : Callable [[], T ], alias : str | None = None , ) -> T Field ( * , alias : str , min_length : int | None = None , max_length : int | None = None , pattern : str | None = None , ge : float | Decimal | None = None , le : float | Decimal | None = None , gt : float | Decimal | None = None , lt : float | Decimal | None = None , one_of : Sequence [ Any ] | None = None , max_digits : int | None = None , decimal_places : int | None = None , multiple_of : int | Decimal | None = None , strip : bool | None = None , lower : bool | None = None , upper : bool | None = None , format : str | None = None , discriminator : str | None = None , description : str | None = None , examples : Sequence [ Any ] | None = None , deprecated : bool | None = None , ) -> Any Field ( * , min_length : int | None = None , max_length : int | None = None , pattern : str | None = None , ge : float | Decimal | None = None , le : float | Decimal | None = None , gt : float | Decimal | None = None , lt : float | Decimal | None = None , one_of : Sequence [ Any ] | None = None , max_digits : int | None = None , decimal_places : int | None = None , multiple_of : int | Decimal | None = None , strip : bool | None = None , lower : bool | None = None , upper : bool | None = None , format : str | None = None , alias : str | None = None , discriminator : str | None = None , description : str | None = None , examples : Sequence [ Any ] | None = None , deprecated : bool | None = None , ) -> FieldInfo Field ( ** options : Any ) -> Any Declare constraints (inside Annotated ) or a default factory. tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list) gives a per-instance default; title: Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1)] adds constraints. hinoki.schema.Invalid ¶ Invalid ( code : str , message : str , * , path : str = '' ) Bases: Exception Raised by a check to refuse a value: a stable code , a readable message and optionally the path it concerns (default: the field the check is attached to, or the object itself). hinoki.schema.Unset ¶ Type of UNSET : a field that was absent from the input (PATCH). hinoki.schema.field_check ¶ field_check ( * names : str ) -> Callable [[ F ], F ] Mark a method as a check on one or more fields: def ok(self, value) . It runs after the structural validation succeeded, so value already has the declared type, and may read the other fields through self . Raise Invalid(code, message) to refuse; it never changes the value. Checks are synchronous and must not do I/O: a rule that needs the database belongs in an operation, not in a schema. hinoki.schema.field_normalize ¶ field_normalize ( name : str ) -> Callable [[ F ], F ] Mark a typed field canonicalizer: def trim(self, value: str) -> str . Methods run synchronously after structural validation and return a replacement string; raise Invalid only from a check hook to reject. hinoki.schema.object_check ¶ object_check ( function : F ) -> F Mark a method as a check on the whole object: def ok(self) . Runs after every field check passed or failed (all problems are reported together). hinoki.schema.before_validate ¶ before_validate ( function : F ) -> F Mark a classmethod or staticmethod that reshapes raw wire input: def prepare(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] . It runs on the decoded mapping, before any structural validation, for the schema and for every schema nested in it (lists, dicts, tuples, optionals and discriminated variants). Return the mapping to validate. The hook gets a shallow copy: replace nested values instead of mutating them, or the caller's input changes. Raise Invalid(code, message) to refuse; a KeyError , TypeError , ValueError , IndexError or AttributeError caused by unexpected input answers as invalid_input . The input is untrusted: check types before relying on them, stay synchronous and do no I/O. Plain unions of schemas that use it are refused: use a discriminator. hinoki.computed.computed_field ¶ computed_field ( function : Callable [[ Any ], T ]) -> T computed_field ( * , alias : str | None = None , description : str | None = None , examples : Sequence [ Any ] | None = None , ) -> Callable [[ Callable [[ Any ], T ]], T ] computed_field ( function : Callable [ ... , Any ] | None = None , / , * , alias : str | None = None , description : str | None = None , examples : Sequence [ Any ] | None = None , ) -> Any Declare a read-only value derived from the other fields of a Schema . @computed_field def full_name(self) -> str reads like an attribute, is written by dump() and by JSON responses after the declared fields, and is documented as a readOnly property. It is never accepted as input and never stored. The return annotation gives its OpenAPI type; the method must be synchronous, take no arguments and not do I/O. hinoki.fields.SecretStr ¶ SecretStr ( value : str ) A string that never shows itself: repr , str , dump() and JSON responses give ********** ; get_secret_value() returns the text. hinoki.errors.ValidationError ¶ ValidationError ( details : list [ ErrorDetail ]) Bases: Exception Input does not match a schema. details lists every problem found. hinoki.fields.UNSET module-attribute ¶ UNSET = Unset () hinoki.derive.derive ¶ derive ( model : type [ Model ] | None = None , * , only : tuple [ str , ... ] | None = None , exclude : tuple [ str , ... ] | None = None , partial : bool | tuple [ str , ... ] = False , ) -> Callable [[ type [ S ]], type [ S ]] Derive selected fields from model into a Schema subclass. The keyword-only form is retained for one compatibility cycle and is deprecated; it requires the legacy model= Schema class keyword.

docs.text: field_check ( * names : str ) -> Callable [[ F ], F ] Mark a method as a check on one or more fields: def ok(self, value) . It runs after the structural validation succeeded, so value already has the declared type, and may read the other fields through self . Raise Invalid(code, message) to refuse; it never changes the value. Checks are synchronous and must not do I/O: a rule that needs the database belongs in an operation, not in a schema.
docs.title: field_check

docs.text: field_normalize ( name : str ) -> Callable [[ F ], F ] Mark a typed field canonicalizer: def trim(self, value: str) -> str . Methods run synchronously after structural validation and return a replacement string; raise Invalid only from a check hook to reject.
docs.title: field_normalize

docs.text: object_check ( function : F ) -> F Mark a method as a check on the whole object: def ok(self) . Runs after every field check passed or failed (all problems are reported together).
docs.title: object_check

docs.text: before_validate ( function : F ) -> F Mark a classmethod or staticmethod that reshapes raw wire input: def prepare(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] . It runs on the decoded mapping, before any structural validation, for the schema and for every schema nested in it (lists, dicts, tuples, optionals and discriminated variants). Return the mapping to validate. The hook gets a shallow copy: replace nested values instead of mutating them, or the caller's input changes. Raise Invalid(code, message) to refuse; a KeyError , TypeError , ValueError , IndexError or AttributeError caused by unexpected input answers as invalid_input . The input is untrusted: check types before relying on them, stay synchronous and do no I/O. Plain unions of schemas that use it are refused: use a discriminator.
docs.title: before_validate

It is never accepted as input and never stored. The return annotation gives its OpenAPI type; the method must be synchronous, take no arguments and not do I/O.

The endpoint answers only application/json POSTs and refuses a request that carries an Origin outside allowed_origins (browsers send one; agents and CLI clients do not) or Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site : this keeps a web page from driving the tools with the user's cookie and covers the MCP DNS-rebinding rule. docs.text: Core API: application, routing and HTTP ¶ from hinoki import Hinoki, RouteGroup, Mount, http, errors and from hinoki.project import manifest_routes . Guides: function-based APIs , class-based APIs , register routes , errors . hinoki.app.Hinoki ¶ Hinoki ( * , settings : object | None = None , include : Sequence [ Includable ] | None = None , modules : Sequence [ Module | type [ Module ]] = (), commands : Sequence [ Command | type [ Command ]] = (), on_startup : Sequence [ Hook ] = (), on_shutdown : Sequence [ Hook ] = (), startup_url : str | None = None , runtime : RuntimeConfig | None = None , title : str | None = None , version : str | None = None , openapi_url : str | Unset | None = UNSET , docs_url : str | Unset | None = UNSET , redoc_url : str | Unset | None = UNSET , rules : RuleSet | None = None , enforce_rules : bool = True , waivers : str | Path | None = None , parsers : Sequence [ Parser ] | None = None , renderers : Sequence [ Renderer ] | None = None , middleware : Sequence [ Middleware ] = (), ) A Hinoki application. Registering routes builds the native router; nothing connects to anything, so factories returning Hinoki are safe to import and call. The instance is itself an ASGI callable ( granian --interface asgi module:app ); the first call freezes the declarations. on_startup and on_shutdown list functions taking the worker's ModuleContext ( async def or def ). Startup hooks run once per worker after the modules have started; shutdown hooks run before they are closed, and only after a startup that completed. startup_url optionally reserves a public GET/HEAD endpoint that returns {"status": "ok"} after worker startup. It reports startup completion, not application, database, or event-loop health. waivers names the owner's waiver file applied to the startup rules; it must exist. Without it, hinoki-rules.toml at the project root is used. settings instance-attribute ¶ settings = settings middleware instance-attribute ¶ middleware = check_middleware ( middleware ) waiver_file instance-attribute ¶ waiver_file : Path | None = ( None if waivers is None else Path ( waivers ) ) routes property ¶ routes : tuple [ Route , ... ] startup_url property ¶ startup_url : str | None The fixed startup-probe path, if one was configured. bindings property ¶ bindings : tuple [ Binding , ... ] modules property ¶ modules : tuple [ Module , ... ] commands property ¶ commands : tuple [ Command , ... ] The app's explicitly registered management commands. on_startup property ¶ on_startup : tuple [ Hook , ... ] Startup hooks, fixed when the application is constructed. on_shutdown property ¶ on_shutdown : tuple [ Hook , ... ] Shutdown hooks, fixed when the application is constructed. admin_settings ¶ admin_settings () -> AdminSettings | None The app's admin settings group, or None without built-in settings. now ¶ now ( clock : Clock = utc_now ) -> datetime Return an aware datetime in this application's configured timezone. settings_database ¶ settings_database ( declared : list [ Module ], ) -> DatabaseModule | None The database module implied by a database: DatabaseSettings field in the settings, unless the application declares its own. module_of ¶ module_of ( module : Module | type [ Module ]) -> Module An instance as given, or a class built from this app's settings. include ¶ include ( * items : Includable ) -> None Register decorated functions, API subclasses and objects that expose an api() (the admin). Lists and tuples of those are flattened, so a feature package can export one routes list, and Mount(prefix, ...) places a feature under a path chosen here. All-or-nothing per call: on conflict the application is unchanged. routes_of staticmethod ¶ routes_of ( item : object ) -> list [ Route ] The routes an item declares: an API class, a decorated function, or an object exposing api() (the admin). inherited_parsers ¶ inherited_parsers ( route : Route ) -> tuple [ Parser , ... ] Parsers for an action without its own: the application's, unless an upload action needs multipart and they do not include it. with_defaults ¶ with_defaults ( route : Route ) -> Route The route with this application's default parsers/renderers filled in where the action did not choose its own. install ¶ install ( * modules : Module ) -> None Install modules and include their APIs. The whole graph (names, requirements, cycles) is validated here, so a broken graph fails in the factory, not in a worker. Nothing opens. lookup ¶ lookup ( method : str , path : str ) -> Found | MethodNotAllowed | None Distinguish a match, a wrong method and an unknown path. HEAD resolves through a matching GET route. Method-not-allowed results advertise HEAD whenever GET is available for the path. resolve ¶ resolve ( method : str , path : str ) -> tuple [ Route , dict [ str , str ]] | None Find the action for a request line; None if unknown or the method is not allowed (use lookup to tell them apart). openapi ¶ openapi () -> dict [ str , Any ] The OpenAPI 3.1 document for the registered routes. asgi ¶ asgi () -> ASGIAdapter The ASGI adapter for this worker; builds and validates bindings once. enforce ¶ enforce () -> None Fail with every startup-rule violation when rules are enforced. With enforce_rules=False the diagnostics are only logged. The owner's waivers apply as in hinoki check : waivers= when given, else the project's hinoki-rules.toml . An invalid waiver file always fails. error_handler ¶ error_handler ( kind : type [ Exception ]) -> ErrorRegistrar Decorator: answer kind with a function of the exception that returns the APIError to send. It returns the function unchanged. @app.error_handler(stripe.CardError) def card_error(error: stripe.CardError) -> errors.APIError: return errors.APIError(error.user_message, status=402) Errors that already are APIError subclasses need no handler. hinoki.api.API ¶ Base class for a resource: several methods, standard or custom. class Posts(API, path='/posts') . Instances hold no per-request state; methods declared with @http.get / @http.post /... become actions. prefix class-attribute ¶ prefix : str = '' routes classmethod ¶ routes () -> list [ Route ] Routes of this class with the prefix applied, in definition order. Members are resolved by name, most derived class first, so an override without a decorator removes the inherited route. apply_replacements classmethod ¶ apply_replacements ( found : list [ Route ]) -> list [ Route ] Drop the routes that another route names in replaces= . declared_route classmethod ¶ declared_route ( name : str , member : object ) -> Route | None mount classmethod ¶ mount ( route : Route ) -> Route hinoki.routing.RouteGroup ¶ RouteGroup ( prefix : str = "" , * , access : Access | None = None , atomic : bool = False , errors : Sequence [ type [ APIError ]] = (), ) A function-based route group with a shared path prefix and defaults. Decorated functions belong to this group and the group can be included once in a Hinoki application. Use API for class-based resources. tasks = RouteGroup("/tasks", access=member_only, atomic=True, errors=(NotFound,)) @tasks.get("/") # GET /tasks async def listing(...): ... @tasks.post("/", status=201) # POST /tasks, atomic=True async def create(...): ... @tasks.get("/health", access=None) # public on purpose, overriding the group prefix is prepended to every path ( "/" means the prefix itself), access is the default policy (pass access=None on an action to make it public), atomic=True makes POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE transactional unless the action says atomic=False , and errors are added to each action's own. The result is an ordinary action: rules, OpenAPI and the MCP see no difference. prefix instance-attribute ¶ prefix = prefix access instance-attribute ¶ access = access atomic instance-attribute ¶ atomic = atomic errors instance-attribute ¶ errors = tuple ( errors ) handlers property ¶ handlers : tuple [ Callable [ ... , object ], ... ] The decorated handlers in declaration order. declare ¶ declare ( method : str , path : str , options : dict [ str , Any ] ) -> RouteDeclaration get ¶ get ( path : str , ** options : Any ) -> _GroupRouteDeclaration post ¶ post ( path : str , ** options : Any ) -> _GroupRouteDeclaration put ¶ put ( path : str , ** options : Any ) -> _GroupRouteDeclaration patch ¶ patch ( path : str , ** options : Any ) -> _GroupRouteDeclaration delete ¶ delete ( path : str , ** options : Any ) -> _GroupRouteDeclaration query ¶ query ( path : str , ** options : Any ) -> _GroupRouteDeclaration hinoki.routing.Includable ¶ Includable = ( type [ API ] | Callable [ ... , object ] | RouteGroup | Mount | ExposesRoutes | Sequence [ Includable ] ) What Hinoki(include=[...]) and app.include(...) accept: an API class, a decorated function, a RouteGroup , a Mount , an object with api() (the admin) or a list or tuple of those. hinoki.routing.Mount ¶ Mount ( prefix : str , * items : object ) Places routes under a path prefix chosen where the application is declared. Hinoki(include=[ health, Mount("/tasks", tasks.routes), Mount("/billing", billing.routes), ]) The feature keeps paths relative to itself ( / and /{id} ) and the root declaration shows where each feature lives. Items are anything include accepts, including lists and other mounts; prefixes join outside in. prefix instance-attribute ¶ prefix = prefix items instance-attribute ¶ items = items pagination : PageNumberPagination | None = None , replaces : str = "" , parsers : tuple [ Parser , ... ] = DEFAULT_PARSERS , renderers : tuple [ Renderer , ... ] = DEFAULT_RENDERERS , errors : tuple [ type [ APIError ], ... ] = (), validate_response : bool = True , rate_limit : RateLimitPolicy | None = None , middleware : tuple [ Middleware , ... ] = (), ) Declared contract of one action, before it is bound to an application. method instance-attribute ¶ method : str path instance-attribute ¶ path : str handler instance-attribute ¶ handler : Callable [ ... , object ] status instance-attribute ¶ status : int access instance-attribute ¶ access : Access | None atomic instance-attribute ¶ atomic : bool owner class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ owner : type | None = None pagination class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ pagination : PageNumberPagination | None = None replaces class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ replaces : str = '' parsers class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ parsers : tuple [ Parser , ... ] = DEFAULT_PARSERS renderers class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ renderers : tuple [ Renderer , ... ] = DEFAULT_RENDERERS errors class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ errors : tuple [ type [ APIError ], ... ] = () validate_response class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ validate_response : bool = True rate_limit class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ rate_limit : RateLimitPolicy | None = None middleware class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ middleware : tuple [ Middleware , ... ] = () is_async property ¶ is_async : bool name property ¶ name : str hinoki.project.manifest_routes ¶ manifest_routes ( start : Path | None = None , ) -> list [ Includable ] The routes hinoki.toml declares: the project's, then each app's at its prefix, for Hinoki(include=manifest_routes()) . The manifest is found from start , by default the directory of the calling file (the working directory when the caller has no file), upwards. Outside a project this raises ProjectError . For model-backed route generation, see Generate CRUD routes and the CRUD API reference . HTTP method decorators ¶ Import the namespace and decorate actions: from hinoki import http , then @http.get(...) . The names are not available at the top level of hinoki . hinoki.http.get ¶ get ( path : str , * , status : int = 200 , access : Access | None = None , atomic : bool = False , pagination : PageNumberPagination | None = None , replaces : str = "" , parsers : Sequence [ Parser ] | None = None , renderers : Sequence [ Renderer ] | None = None , errors : Sequence [ type [ APIError ]] = (), validate_response : bool = True , rate_limit : RateLimitPolicy | None = None , middleware : Sequence [ Middleware ] = (), ) -> RouteDeclaration Declare a GET action. errors lists the APIError subclasses the action may raise; each carries its own status and code, which OpenAPI and the MCP tool description then show. hinoki.http.post ¶ post ( path : str , * , status : int = 200 , access : Access | None = None , atomic : bool = False , pagination : PageNumberPagination | None = None , replaces : str = "" , parsers : Sequence [ Parser ] | None = None , renderers : Sequence [ Renderer ] | None = None , errors : Sequence [ type [ APIError ]] = (), validate_response : bool = True , rate_limit : RateLimitPolicy | None = None , middleware : Sequence [ Middleware ] = (), ) -> RouteDeclaration Declare a POST action. errors lists the APIError subclasses the action may raise; each carries its own status and code, which OpenAPI and the MCP tool description then show. hinoki.http.put ¶ put ( path : str , * , status : int = 200 , access : Access | None = None , atomic : bool = False , pagination : PageNumberPagination | None = None , replaces : str = "" , parsers : Sequence [ Parser ] | None = None , renderers : Sequence [ Renderer ] | None = None , errors : Sequence [ type [ APIError ]] = (), validate_response : bool = True , rate_limit : RateLimitPolicy | None = None , middleware : Sequence [ Middleware ] = (), ) -> RouteDeclaration Declare a PUT action. errors lists the APIError subclasses the action may raise; each carries its own status and code, which OpenAPI and the MCP tool description then show. hinoki.http.delete ¶ delete ( path : str , * , status : int = 200 , access : Access | None = None , atomic : bool = False , pagination : PageNumberPagination | None = None , replaces : str = "" , parsers : Sequence [ Parser ] | None = None , renderers : Sequence [ Renderer ] | None = None , errors : Sequence [ type [ APIError ]] = (), validate_response : bool = True , rate_limit : RateLimitPolicy | None = None , middleware : Sequence [ Middleware ] = (), ) -> RouteDeclaration Declare a DELETE action. errors lists the APIError subclasses the action may raise; each carries its own status and code, which OpenAPI and the MCP tool description then show. hinoki.http.query ¶ query ( path : str , * , status : int = 200 , access : Access | None = None , atomic : bool = False , pagination : PageNumberPagination | None = None , replaces : str = "" , parsers : Sequence [ Parser ] | None = None , renderers : Sequence [ Renderer ] | None = None , errors : Sequence [ type [ APIError ]] = (), validate_response : bool = True , rate_limit : RateLimitPolicy | None = None , middleware : Sequence [ Middleware ] = (), ) -> RouteDeclaration Declare a QUERY action: a safe, idempotent request that carries a body (a search too large or too structured for a query string). It binds its body like POST and is never wrapped in a transaction unless asked. errors lists the APIError subclasses the action may raise; each carries its own status and code, which OpenAPI and the MCP tool description then show. Request, response and errors ¶ The types are available from hinoki.http , from hinoki , or from their modules hinoki.http.request and hinoki.http.response . hinoki.http.request.Request ¶ Request ( * , method : str , path : str , scheme : str , host : str , client : tuple [ str , int ] | None , headers : Mapping [ str , str ], query : Mapping [ str , list [ str ]], body : bytes , path_params : Mapping [ str , str ], user : Any , request_id : str , parsers : Sequence [ Parser ] = DEFAULT_PARSERS , ) One HTTP request. Never mutate it; it is shared with the whole call. method instance-attribute ¶ method = method path instance-attribute ¶ path = path scheme instance-attribute ¶ scheme = scheme host instance-attribute ¶ host = host client instance-attribute ¶ client = client headers instance-attribute ¶ headers = ( headers if isinstance ( headers , Headers ) else Headers ( headers ) ) GET instance-attribute ¶ GET = QueryDict ( query ) COOKIES instance-attribute ¶ COOKIES = core . parse_cookie_header ( self . headers . get ( "cookie" , "" ) ) body instance-attribute ¶ body = body path_params instance-attribute ¶ path_params = dict ( path_params ) user instance-attribute ¶ user = user request_id instance-attribute ¶ request_id = request_id parsers instance-attribute ¶ parsers = tuple ( parsers ) cached instance-attribute ¶ cached : Parsed | None = None content_type property ¶ content_type : str Media type without parameters, lower-case ("" when absent). data property ¶ data : object The parsed body (JSON value, or form fields as text). POST property ¶ POST : QueryDict Form fields; empty when the body is not a form. FILES property ¶ FILES : MultiDict [ UploadedFile ] Uploaded files of a multipart body; empty otherwise. parsed ¶ parsed () -> Parsed The body through the parser for its content type, once; raises InvalidBody (415 for an unlisted type, 400 for a malformed body). accepts_form ¶ accepts_form () -> bool hinoki.http.response.Response ¶ Response ( status : int = 200 , body : bytes | str = b "" , headers : Headers = (), content_type : str | None = None , ) Status, headers and body chosen by the handler. status instance-attribute ¶ status = status body instance-attribute ¶ body = raw headers instance-attribute ¶ headers = [ encode_header ( name , value ) for name , value in items ] raw classmethod ¶ raw ( status : int , body : bytes , headers : Sequence [ tuple [ bytes , bytes ]], ) -> Response A response from encoded parts, checked like one built from text: a framing or server header, a bad name or a CR/LF in a value raise ValueError . The name must be a token and the value cookie-safe (no space, quote, comma, semicolon or backslash); encode richer data yourself. hinoki.access.Access dataclass ¶ Access ( auth : BaseAuth [ Any ], permissions : Iterable [ str ] = () ) Which provider authenticates an action and which permissions it requires. Access(auth=tokens, permissions=["posts:write"]) . Declaring an Access does not protect anything by itself: only actions that name it are protected. Enforcement belongs to the request pipeline. auth instance-attribute ¶ auth : BaseAuth [ Any ] permissions class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ permissions : frozenset [ str ] = field ( default_factory = frozenset ) hinoki.errors.APIError ¶ APIError ( message : str | None = None , * , code : str | None = None , status : int | None = None , details : list [ dict [ str , Any ]] | None = None , headers : dict [ str , str ] | None = None , ) Bases: Exception An error with a public HTTP representation. Subclasses set status , code and message ; an instance may override them, which is how a handler answers with a status of its own: APIError("Card declined", status=402, code="card_declined") . details is public data, never internal state. hinoki.errors.BadRequest ¶ BadRequest ( message : str | None = None , * , code : str | None = None , status : int | None = None , details : list [ dict [ str , Any ]] | None = None , headers : dict [ str , str ] | None = None , ) Bases: APIError hinoki.errors.Unauthorized ¶ Unauthorized ( message : str | None = None , * , code : str | None = None , status : int | None = None , details : list [ dict [ str , Any ]] | None = None , headers : dict [ str , str ] | None = None , ) Bases: APIError hinoki.errors.Forbidden ¶ Forbidden ( message : str | None = None , * , code : str | None = None , status : int | None = None , details : list [ dict [ str , Any ]] | None = None , headers : dict [ str , str ] | None = None , ) Bases: APIError hinoki.errors.NotFound ¶ NotFound ( message : str | None = None , * , code : str | None = None , status : int | None = None , details : list [ dict [ str , Any ]] | None = None , headers : dict [ str , str ] | None = None , ) Bases: APIError hinoki.errors.Conflict ¶ Conflict ( message : str | None = None , * , code : str | None = None , status : int | None = None , details : list [ dict [ str , Any ]] | None = None , headers : dict [ str , str ] | None = None , ) Bases: APIError hinoki.errors.TooManyRequests ¶ TooManyRequests ( retry_after : int , message : str | None = None , * , code : str | None = None , ) Bases: APIError The one error a rate_limit policy may raise to refuse a request. retry_after is a whole number of seconds from 1 to 86,400, sent as Retry-After ; anything else is refused when the error is created. hinoki.errors.UniqueConflict ¶ UniqueConflict ( message : str | None = None , * , code : str | None = None , status : int | None = None , details : list [ dict [ str , Any ]] | None = None , headers : dict [ str , str ] | None = None , ) Bases: Conflict A unique value is already in use: the answer to a UniqueViolation . hinoki.errors.ObjectNotFound ¶ Bases: ModelError A query that must return one row returned none. Each model has its own subclass as Model.NotFound ; HTTP maps it to 404. hinoki.errors.ErrorRegistry ¶ ErrorRegistry () Maps exception classes to handlers; the most specific class wins. is_builtin ¶ is_builtin ( exc : Exception ) -> bool Whether only synchronous built-in translations can answer exc : no application handler matches it. translate_builtin ¶ translate_builtin ( exc : Exception ) -> APIError | None translate for an exception is_builtin accepted, without a coroutine. translate async ¶ translate ( exc : Exception ) -> APIError | None The public error for exc , or None if nothing handles it. A handler that fails or returns something else is treated as unhandled. Rate limits ¶ hinoki.ratelimit.RateLimitPolicy ¶ Bases: Protocol Anything with a check method, def or async def . A sync check runs on the bounded executor and must use sync clients with finite timeouts; an async one runs on the event loop. hinoki.ratelimit.RateLimitContext dataclass ¶ RateLimitContext ( method : str , route : str , client : str | None , caller : Caller [ Any ] | None , lookup : Callable [[ type [ Any ]], Any ], ) What a policy may decide from: no headers, credentials, body or query. resource ¶ resource ( kind : type [ T ]) -> T The worker-owned resource of this type that a module provided (for example a Redis client or the Database ); LookupError if none.

docs.text: Hinoki ( * , settings : object | None = None , include : Sequence [ Includable ] | None = None , modules : Sequence [ Module | type [ Module ]] = (), commands : Sequence [ Command | type [ Command ]] = (), on_startup : Sequence [ Hook ] = (), on_shutdown : Sequence [ Hook ] = (), startup_url : str | None = None , runtime : RuntimeConfig | None = None , title : str | None = None , version : str | None = None , openapi_url : str | Unset | None = UNSET , docs_url : str | Unset | None = UNSET , redoc_url : str | Unset | None = UNSET , rules : RuleSet | None = None , enforce_rules : bool = True , waivers : str | Path | None = None , parsers : Sequence [ Parser ] | None = None , renderers : Sequence [ Renderer ] | None = None , middleware : Sequence [ Middleware ] = (), ) A Hinoki application. Registering routes builds the native router; nothing connects to anything, so factories returning Hinoki are safe to import and call. The instance is itself an ASGI callable ( granian --interface asgi module:app ); the first call freezes the declarations. on_startup and on_shutdown list functions taking the worker's ModuleContext ( async def or def ). Startup hooks run once per worker after the modules have started; shutdown hooks run before they are closed, and only after a startup that completed. startup_url optionally reserves a public GET/HEAD endpoint that returns {"status": "ok"} after worker startup. It reports startup completion, not application, database, or event-loop health. waivers names the owner's waiver file applied to the startup rules; it must exist. Without it, hinoki-rules.toml at the project root is used.

docs.text: RouteGroup ( prefix : str = "" , * , access : Access | None = None , atomic : bool = False , errors : Sequence [ type [ APIError ]] = (), ) A function-based route group with a shared path prefix and defaults. Decorated functions belong to this group and the group can be included once in a Hinoki application. Use API for class-based resources. tasks = RouteGroup("/tasks", access=member_only, atomic=True, errors=(NotFound,)) @tasks.get("/") # GET /tasks async def listing(...): ... @tasks.post("/", status=201) # POST /tasks, atomic=True async def create(...): ... @tasks.get("/health", access=None) # public on purpose, overriding the group prefix is prepended to every path ( "/" means the prefix itself), access is the default policy (pass access=None on an action to make it public), atomic=True makes POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE transactional unless the action says atomic=False , and errors are added to each action's own. The result is an ordinary action: rules, OpenAPI and the MCP see no difference.

docs.text: Tutorial ¶ Follow the Tracker, an API where members keep their own tasks, one layer per chapter. Each chapter walks through files of the checked-in example in examples/tracker and runs its commands, so every step runs as shown. Chapter 8 then adds an app to your own project. Chapter It covers You learn 1. Models tables, an index, a default order models and migrations 2. Schemas what clients send and receive strict validation, derived schemas 3. Operations the business rules ownership inside the statement 4. Endpoints the HTTP layer access, transactions, declared errors 5. Rules checks that keep the layers apart hinoki check 6. Run and test it settings, a server, tests hinoki dev , the test client 7. Validate input normalizers and checks field and cross-field errors 8. Projects and apps an app in your own project hinoki app create , planned migrations Chapters 1–6 cover the Tracker. Chapter 7 uses standalone examples, and chapter 8 continues the project from the Quick start . The Tracker is one project ( tracker/ : main.py , settings, rules) with one app ( tracker/apps/tracker/ ) that owns the models, schemas, operations, security and endpoints, created the way chapter 8 creates yours. Its layers: api.py HTTP: shapes, status codes, access, transactions ↓ operations.py business rules: plain async functions, no HTTP types ↓ models.py tables and relations Before you start ¶ Install Hinoki . Chapters 1–6 run in the checkout's examples/ directory: cd examples That directory hosts three applications (Notes, Tracker and Blog) under one hinoki.toml , so server and check commands name the application, such as uv run hinoki check tracker.main:app . docs.text: Follow the Tracker, an API where members keep their own tasks, one layer per chapter. Each chapter walks through files of the checked-in example in examples/tracker and runs its commands, so every step runs as shown. Chapter 8 then adds an app to your own project. Chapter It covers You learn 1. Models tables, an index, a default order models and migrations 2. Schemas what clients send and receive strict validation, derived schemas 3. Operations the business rules ownership inside the statement 4. Endpoints the HTTP layer access, transactions, declared errors 5. Rules checks that keep the layers apart hinoki check 6. Run and test it settings, a server, tests hinoki dev , the test client 7. Validate input normalizers and checks field and cross-field errors 8. Projects and apps an app in your own project hinoki app create , planned migrations Chapters 1–6 cover the Tracker. Chapter 7 uses standalone examples, and chapter 8 continues the project from the Quick start . The Tracker is one project ( tracker/ : main.py , settings, rules) with one app ( tracker/apps/tracker/ ) that owns the models, schemas, operations, security and endpoints, created the way chapter 8 creates yours. docs.text: 1. Models ¶ A model declares a table. A relation is loaded only when you ask for it, never as a side effect of reading an attribute. # tracker/apps/tracker/models.py from datetime import datetime from uuid import UUID , uuid4 from hinoki import db from hinoki.orm import Model , OnDelete , field , foreign_key , pk from hinoki.utils import utc_now @db . table ( "tracker_members" ) class Member ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) name : str = field ( max_length = 80 ) token : str = field ( unique = True ) @db . indexed ( "owner_id" , "created_at" ) @db . ordered_by ( "-created_at" , "-id" ) @db . table ( "tracker_tasks" ) class Task ( Model , label = "Task" , plural = "Tasks" ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) owner_id : UUID = foreign_key ( Member , on_delete = OnDelete . RESTRICT , related_name = "tasks" ) title : str = field ( max_length = 120 ) done : bool = False created_at : datetime = field ( default_factory = utc_now ) completed_at : datetime | None = None pk(...) declares the primary key; field(...) adds column options such as max_length and unique . @db.indexed("owner_id", "created_at") adds a composite index. @db.ordered_by(...) sets the order of every query that does not call order_by . foreign_key(Member, ...) stores the owner's id. task.owner is fetched only when a query asks for it. @db.table(...) pins the table name, because a Tracker rule requires it ( chapter 5 ). Without it, Hinoki derives <app>_<models> , as chapter 8 shows. Apply the migrations ¶ A migration is a SQL file generated from the models and checked in beside them. Tracker ships two; the second adds the composite index: -- tracker/apps/tracker/migrations/0002-indexes.sql -- index tracker_tasks (owner_id, created_at) CREATE INDEX "ix_tracker_tasks_owner_id_created_at" ON "tracker_tasks" ( "owner_id" , "created_at" ); From examples/ , list and apply them: uv run hinoki migrations status tracker uv run hinoki migrations apply tracker database: sqlite:///.../examples/.hinoki/local.sqlite3 (from local SQLite default) tracker pending 0001-initial tracker pending 0002-indexes database: sqlite:///.../examples/.hinoki/local.sqlite3 (from local SQLite default) tracker: 0001-initial, 0002-indexes Each command first names the database it uses. With no database configured, that is examples/.hinoki/local.sqlite3 . Migrations run only when you call apply ; an application never migrates at startup. When a model changes, uv run hinoki migrations plan tracker writes the next migration. Review its SQL, then apply it. Recap ¶ A model is a typed class; decorators state table facts such as indexes and order. Migrations are reviewed files, applied by an explicit command. Relations are never loaded implicitly. Next: 2. Schemas .

docs.text: 2. Schemas ¶ A model describes a table; a Schema describes what crosses the API. A column reaches a client only when a schema names it. # tracker/apps/tracker/schemas.py from typing import Annotated from hinoki import Field , Schema , derive from .models import Task class TaskIn ( Schema ): """What a client may set. The owner is the caller, never a field.""" title : Annotated [ str , Field ( min_length = 1 , max_length = 120 )] @derive ( Task , exclude = ( "owner_id" ,)) class TaskOut ( Schema ): """Every column of a task except its owner (derived from the model).""" TaskIn is strict: no coercion, no unknown keys, and every problem is reported with its path. Validation runs in Rust before your code does. TaskOut takes its fields from Task , with the model's types and limits. exclude=("owner_id",) keeps the owner out. Relations are never derived; you name them on purpose. The owner is not a field of TaskIn , so a client cannot choose it. Server values passed to Task.acreate(data, owner_id=...) always win, and a schema never carries the primary key. Schemas also support aliases, computed fields and tagged unions; see discriminated unions . Recap ¶ Input schemas list what a client may send, nothing more. Output schemas can be derived from a model, minus what must stay private. Ownership comes from the caller, never from the request body. Next: 3. Operations .

docs.text: 3. Operations ¶ The rules of the application live in plain async functions. They take the acting member's id and plain values, never a Request , so an endpoint, a command, a test or an admin hook can call them. # tracker/apps/tracker/operations.py from uuid import UUID from hinoki.orm import QuerySet from hinoki.pagination import Page , PageParams from hinoki.utils import utc_now from .errors import DoneTasksAreKept , TaskAlreadyDone from .models import Task from .schemas import TaskIn def mine ( owner_id : UUID ) -> QuerySet [ Task ]: return Task . filter ( owner_id = owner_id ) async def list_tasks ( owner_id : UUID , page : PageParams ) -> Page [ Task ]: return await mine ( owner_id ) . apaginate ( page ) # Task is @ordered_by newest first async def create_task ( owner_id : UUID , data : TaskIn ) -> Task : return await Task . acreate ( data , owner_id = owner_id ) # the server's value wins Writes put the owner in the statement itself: # tracker/apps/tracker/operations.py (continued) async def complete_task ( owner_id : UUID , task_id : UUID ) -> Task : """Mark an own open task done in one statement.""" changed = await Task . aupdate_where ( { "id" : task_id , "owner_id" : owner_id , "done" : False }, { "done" : True , "completed_at" : utc_now ()}, ) if changed : return changed [ 0 ] await mine ( owner_id ) . filter ( id = task_id ) . aget () # missing or not yours: 404 raise TaskAlreadyDone () async def delete_task ( owner_id : UUID , task_id : UUID ) -> None : """Delete an own open task; completed ones are kept.""" removed = await Task . adelete ( id = task_id , owner_id = owner_id , done = False ) if removed : return await mine ( owner_id ) . filter ( id = task_id ) . aget () # missing or not yours: 404 raise DoneTasksAreKept () There is no gap between reading a row, checking its owner and writing it. Another member's task looks exactly like a missing one (404), so nothing leaks. Business failures are named after the rule they report. Each carries its HTTP status (409 for Conflict ) and a stable code: # tracker/apps/tracker/errors.py from hinoki import errors class TaskAlreadyDone ( errors . Conflict ): code = "task_already_done" message = "The task is already done." class DoneTasksAreKept ( errors . Conflict ): code = "done_tasks_are_kept" message = "Completed tasks are kept as a record and cannot be deleted." Recap ¶ Operations hold the rules and know nothing about HTTP. Ownership is part of the WHERE clause, not a separate check. Errors are classes with a status and a stable code. Next: 4. Endpoints .

docs.text: 4. Endpoints ¶ The HTTP layer maps requests to operations and results to responses. It holds no business rule and no SQL. First, who may call. A bearer token resolves to a Member , and the policy names the permission that every task action requires: # tracker/apps/tracker/security.py from hinoki import Access , BearerAuth , Caller , Permission from .models import Member class TrackerPermission ( Permission ): USE = "tasks:use" class MemberTokens ( BearerAuth [ Member ]): async def resolve_token ( self , token : str ) -> Caller [ Member ] | None : member = await Member . aget_or_none ( token = token ) if member is None : return None return Caller ( id = str ( member . id ), user = member , permissions = { TrackerPermission . USE } ) member_only = Access ( auth = MemberTokens (), permissions = [ TrackerPermission . USE ]) Then the actions. A public health check stands alone; a RouteGroup states the path prefix, the policy and the transaction once for the tasks: # tracker/apps/tracker/api.py from uuid import UUID from hinoki import Caller , RouteGroup , Schema , errors , http from hinoki.pagination import Page , PageNumberPagination , PageParams from . import operations from .errors import DoneTasksAreKept , TaskAlreadyDone from .models import Member from .schemas import TaskIn , TaskOut from .security import member_only class Health ( Schema ): status : str @http . get ( "/health" ) def health () -> Health : return Health ( status = "ok" ) tasks = RouteGroup ( "/tasks" , access = member_only , atomic = True ) @tasks . get ( "/" , pagination = PageNumberPagination ( page_size = 10 , max_page_size = 50 )) async def list_tasks ( page : PageParams , caller : Caller [ Member ]) -> Page [ TaskOut ]: """Your tasks, newest first.""" return ( await operations . list_tasks ( caller . user . id , page )) . map ( TaskOut . from_model ) @tasks . post ( "/" , status = 201 ) async def create_task ( data : TaskIn , caller : Caller [ Member ]) -> TaskOut : return TaskOut . from_model ( await operations . create_task ( caller . user . id , data )) # tracker/apps/tracker/api.py (continued) @tasks . post ( "/ {task_id} /complete" , errors = ( errors . NotFound , TaskAlreadyDone )) async def complete_task ( task_id : UUID , caller : Caller [ Member ]) -> TaskOut : return TaskOut . from_model ( await operations . complete_task ( caller . user . id , task_id )) @tasks . delete ( "/ {task_id} " , status = 204 , errors = ( errors . NotFound , DoneTasksAreKept )) async def delete_task ( task_id : UUID , caller : Caller [ Member ]) -> None : await operations . delete_task ( caller . user . id , task_id ) access= names a reusable policy. Actions are public unless they name one, so protect on purpose; a rule in the next chapter enforces it. atomic=True runs each write in a transaction. It commits after the response is encoded and rolls back before an error becomes HTTP. errors=(...) declares what an action may raise. The OpenAPI document, the MCP tool description and the strict test client all read it. caller: Caller[Member] is the authenticated caller, typed: caller.user is your Member . TaskOut.from_model(...) converts a row into the response. A handler never returns a model; lists and pages use .map(...) . Declare request: Request as the first parameter only when you need headers, cookies or the raw body. File uploads are covered in upload files . Register the routes ¶ In a project, routes.py lists the groups and hinoki.toml mounts them ( chapter 8 ). Tracker's main.py includes tasks directly, because examples/ hosts three applications ( chapter 6 ). Recap ¶ A RouteGroup states access, transactions and the prefix once. Handlers call operations and convert rows with from_model . Every error an action raises is declared. Next: 5. Rules . In the guides: function-based APIs and class-based APIs .

docs.text: 5. Rules ¶ Rules turn the project's promises into checks. A failure names the rule, the file and the line. # tracker/rules.py from hinoki import Actions , Imports , Models , Schemas , Transactions from hinoki.rules import RuleSet PKG = "tracker" APP = f " { PKG } .apps.tracker" # the app that owns the models, operations and api tracker_rules = RuleSet ( Actions . require_access ( match = f " { PKG } .*" , except_ = [ f " { APP } .api.health" ]), Actions . require_permissions ( match = f " { PKG } .*" , except_ = [ f " { APP } .api.health" ]), Actions . forbid_model_responses ( match = f " { PKG } .*" ), Actions . require_return_type ( match = f " { PKG } .*" ), Actions . require_pagination ( match = f " { PKG } .*" ), # The MCP endpoint dispatches other actions, which have their own transactions. Transactions . require_atomic ( except_ = [ "hinoki.ai.mcpapp.*" ]), Schemas . forbid_exposure ( "token" ), Schemas . require_string_limits (), # Tables are pinned, and a foreign key is always indexed. Models . require_explicit_table ( match = f " { PKG } .*" ), Models . require_foreign_key_index ( match = f " { PKG } .*" ), # The direction of dependencies: api -> operations -> models. Imports . forbid ( source = f " { APP } .models" , target = f " { APP } .operations" ), Imports . forbid ( source = f " { APP } .models" , target = f " { APP } .api" ), Imports . forbid ( source = f " { APP } .operations" , target = f " { APP } .api" ), ) The application passes them to Hinoki(rules=tracker_rules) , so a worker refuses to start while one is violated. Run the check ¶ From examples/ : uv run hinoki check tracker.main:app 13 rule(s): 0 violated, 0 unverifiable, 0 waived The check reads the rules from the application and scans the tracker package for the import rules. Break a rule ¶ Take create_task out of the group's transaction by adding atomic=False to its decorator, then run the check again: tracker/apps/tracker/api.py:29: HNK-TXN-001 [violated] POST /tasks (create_task) does not declare atomic=True fix: add atomic=True to the action (or declare it on a RouteGroup(..., atomic=True) group) 13 rule(s): 1 violated, 0 unverifiable, 0 waived The command exits with status 1. Remove atomic=False to restore the check. Waivers ¶ An accepted exception is a waiver in hinoki-rules.toml , with a reason, an owner and a bounded target. hinoki check and application startup apply the same waivers. The project owner writes waivers; tools and agents read them but never edit them to make a check pass. Recap ¶ Rules are Python values in the project, checked by hinoki check and at startup. Each failure has a stable id, a location and a fix. Exceptions are explicit, owned waivers. Next: 6. Run and test it .

docs.text: 6. Run and test it ¶ Settings ¶ Settings are a typed class. Tracker declares a database; with no value set it is local SQLite. Each field of DatabaseSettings is a TRACKER_DATABASE__<FIELD> variable, two underscores between the group and the field, so TRACKER_DATABASE__URL selects another database ( Configure a database ): # tracker/settings.py from hinoki import settings class TrackerSettings ( settings . AppSettings , prefix = "TRACKER_" ): database : settings . DatabaseSettings main.py declares the application at module level, with its rules, routes and an MCP tool: # tracker/main.py from hinoki import Hinoki from hinoki.ai.mcpapp import expose_as_mcp from .apps.tracker import api from .apps.tracker.security import member_only from .rules import tracker_rules from .settings import TrackerSettings app = Hinoki ( settings = TrackerSettings , title = "Tracker" , openapi_url = "/openapi.json" , docs_url = "/docs" , redoc_url = "/redoc" , include = [ api . health , api . tasks ], rules = tracker_rules , ) # The MCP endpoint exposes only this action and uses the caller's own token. app . include ( * expose_as_mcp ( app , tools = [ f " { api . __name__ } .list_tasks" ], access = member_only ) ) Hinoki(settings=TrackerSettings) reads the TRACKER_* variables at import; nothing connects until a worker starts. From examples/ , in a second terminal: uv run hinoki shell >>> await Member . acreate ( name = "Ann" , token = "ann-dev-token" ) Leave the shell with Ctrl-D, then call the API with the token: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/tasks \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer ann-dev-token' \ -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"title":"Write the report"}' curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/tasks -H 'Authorization: Bearer ann-dev-token' The first call answers 201 with the new task, the second a page with it. Without the header both answer 401 . Test it ¶ The application reads its settings at import, so the test configuration sets the database variable first. Run it from the repository root against a disposable database, which the fixture empties first: export HINOKI_TEST_DATABASE_URL = sqlite://./.hinoki/tracker-test.sqlite3 uv run pytest tests/trackertest.py strict_errors=True fails a test when an action answers an error it did not declare. For tests without async , use SyncClient . Recap ¶ Settings are typed and read from prefixed environment variables. hinoki dev serves with reload; migrations stay a separate step. Test operations directly and the stack with ASGIClient . Next: 7. Validate input .
