docs.text: 7. Validate input ¶ A Schema validates in three steps, all before your code runs: built-in constraints reject invalid input, normalizers make valid strings canonical, and checks reject values that are valid but not acceptable. Normalize and check fields ¶ # registration.py from typing import Annotated from hinoki import ( Field , Invalid , Schema , errors , field_check , field_normalize , object_check , ) class Registration ( Schema ): username : Annotated [ str , Field ( min_length = 3 , max_length = 32 , pattern = r "[a-z0-9_]+" )] email : Annotated [ str , Field ( format = "email" )] password : Annotated [ str , Field ( min_length = 12 )] confirmation : str @field_normalize ( "email" ) def lowercase_email ( self , value : str ) -> str : return value . lower () @field_check ( "password" ) def reject_common_password ( self , value : str ) -> None : if value . lower () in { "password12345" , "qwerty123456" }: raise Invalid ( "common_password" , "choose a less common password" ) @object_check def passwords_match ( self ) -> None : if self . password != self . confirmation : raise Invalid ( "password_mismatch" , "passwords do not match" , path = "confirmation" ) # registration.py (continued) user = Registration . validate ( { "username" : "mari_23" , "email" : "Mari@Example.test" , "password" : "correct-horse-battery" , "confirmation" : "correct-horse-battery" , } ) assert user . email == "mari@example.test" try : Registration . validate ( { "username" : "mari_23" , "email" : "mari@example.test" , "password" : "password12345" , "confirmation" : "different-password" , } ) except errors . ValidationError as error : for detail in error . details : print ( detail . path , detail . code , detail . message ) password common_password choose a less common password confirmation password_mismatch passwords do not match Constraints come first: min_length , max_length , pattern , and format= ( email , url , slug , hex_color ); numbers take gt , ge , lt and le , and one_of fixes the allowed values. A failed constraint stops validation of that field. @field_normalize receives a valid string and returns a str ; the result is checked against the same constraints. It also runs for Schema(...) and from_model(...) . @field_check sees the final value of one field, @object_check the whole schema. Both raise Invalid(code, message) and return None . Normalizers and checks are synchronous and do no I/O. A rule that needs the database, such as "this email is not registered yet", belongs in an operation, where it can be race-safe. Ignore unknown fields ¶ Unknown fields are rejected by default. For an external payload that adds metadata you do not use, discard unknown keys on that Schema : # webhooks.py from hinoki import Schema , SchemaConfig , SchemaExtra class Webhook ( Schema , config = SchemaConfig ( extra = SchemaExtra . IGNORE )): event_id : str revision : int event = Webhook . validate ( { "event_id" : "evt-1" , "revision" : 2 , "provider_data" : { "trace" : "abc" }} ) assert event . dump () == { "event_id" : "evt-1" , "revision" : 2 } Declared fields stay strict, and ignored keys are never stored or dumped. Constructor keywords and from_model(..., **extra) stay strict too, and each nested Schema applies its own policy. Validate model writes ¶ Data can also reach a table without an HTTP Schema : from a management command or the admin. Put the same constraints on the model: # catalog/models.py from uuid import UUID , uuid4 from hinoki import Field from hinoki.orm import Model , field , pk def trimmed ( value : str ) -> None : if value != value . strip (): raise ValueError ( "surrounding whitespace is not allowed" ) class Product ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) sku : str = field ( max_length = 32 , constraints = Field ( min_length = 3 , pattern = r "[A-Z0-9-]+" ) ) name : str = field ( max_length = 120 , validators = ( trimmed ,)) price : float = field ( constraints = Field ( gt = 0 )) The checks run before acreate , asave and queryset aupdate , and their synchronous forms. An invalid write raises ModelValidationError (import it from hinoki.errors ) with structured details and sends no SQL. Rows that are read are not revalidated. See field constraints and validators . Recap ¶ Constraints, then normalizers, then checks; all before the handler. Unknown keys are an error unless a Schema opts out. Model constraints guard writes that bypass HTTP. Next: 8. Projects and apps .

docs.text: 8. Projects and apps ¶ An app is a package with its own models, migrations and routes, registered in hinoki.toml . This chapter adds a billing app to the notes project from the Quick start . Create the app ¶ From the project root: uv run hinoki app create Prompt Default Answer App name billing URL prefix /billing /billing Depends on (none) The command writes the package and registers it: notes/apps/billing/ ├── api.py endpoints of the app ├── routes.py the list of routes served, mounted at the prefix ├── models.py tables of the app └── migrations/ migration history [[apps]] name = "billing" models = "notes.apps.billing.models" migrations = "notes.apps.billing.migrations" routes = "notes.apps.billing.routes:routes" prefix = "/billing" requires = [] Hinoki reads apps only from hinoki.toml ; it never scans installed packages. If billing later references a model of another app, list that app in requires : migrations then run in dependency order. Add a model ¶ # notes/apps/billing/models.py from datetime import datetime from uuid import UUID , uuid4 from hinoki import db from hinoki.orm import Model , field , pk from hinoki.utils import utc_now @db . ordered_by ( "-created_at" ) class Invoice ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) reference : str = field ( max_length = 40 , unique = True ) paid : bool = False created_at : datetime = field ( default_factory = utc_now , index = True ) The table name is derived: billing_invoices , the app followed by the plural model name. @db.table("billing_invoices") pins it, so renaming the class keeps the physical name; the model rules below ask for it. Plan and apply the migration ¶ uv run hinoki migrations plan billing uv run hinoki migrations apply database: sqlite:///…/notes/.hinoki/local.sqlite3 (from local SQLite default) create table billing_invoices wrote …/notes/apps/billing/migrations/0001-create-table-billing-invoices.sql database: sqlite:///…/notes/.hinoki/local.sqlite3 (from local SQLite default) notes: nothing to apply billing: 0001-create-table-billing-invoices plan compares the models with the recorded migration state and writes the next migration; the number and the slug come from the change. Review the .sql file before you apply it. With more than one app, plan needs the app name; apply runs every app in dependency order. Where the data goes apply uses the application's database setting, so the variable that configures the server, such as NOTES_DATABASE__URL , also configures the migrations; plan , status and apply print the database they chose. With no database configured, apply creates .hinoki/local.sqlite3 beside hinoki.toml . HINOKI_DATABASE_URL overrides the setting for one run. If the application cannot be loaded, the commands stop (exit 2) instead of guessing. Migrations never run when the application starts. Check the project ¶ uv run hinoki check uv run pytest 8 rule(s): 0 violated, 0 unverifiable, 0 waived notes/rules.py keeps two model rules commented out: Models.require_explicit_table and Models.require_foreign_key_index . hinoki check sees only the models the application imports, and a model rule that matches no model is unverifiable , which fails the check. Turn them on (and import Models ) once a billing route imports Invoice ; then add @db.table("billing_invoices") above the class, or the check reports: notes/apps/billing/models.py:10: HNK-DB-001 [violated] Invoice uses the derived table name 'billing_invoices' fix: name the table with @db.table(...) or table=... on the model Pinning the derived name changes no table: migrations plan billing then reports no changes . Endpoints for billing go in notes/apps/billing/api.py , and routes.py lists them. The application in notes/main.py includes every app's list with manifest_routes() , which mounts this one at /billing , so paths inside the app never repeat the prefix: # notes/main.py (as hinoki new wrote it) from hinoki import Hinoki from hinoki.project import manifest_routes from notes.rules import project_rules from notes.settings import ProjectSettings app = Hinoki ( settings = ProjectSettings , # NOTES_* variables and .env include = manifest_routes (), # notes/routes.py, then each app's routes at its prefix title = "Notes" , openapi_url = "/openapi.json" , docs_url = "/docs" , rules = project_rules , ) The project's rules require every action to name an Access policy with permissions; build one as in chapter 4 . Recap ¶ hinoki app create writes an app and registers it in hinoki.toml . Table names, migration numbers and slugs are derived; you review the SQL. The manifest sets each app's prefix; code never repeats it.
